scenarios.title: Server status
scenarios.purpose: Uptime, disks, services and network of a production server.
scenarios.excerpt:
New-BGInfo -Theme $look -Target File {
    $tile = @{ SurfaceStyle = 'Glass' }
    $tiles = @(
        if ($server.Available) {
        New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind Terminal -Label 'UPTIME' `
            -Value $uptime `
            -Detail 'Since the September patch window' -Status Ok
        New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind Cpu -Label 'CPU' `
            -Value "$($server.Cpu[-1]) %" -Detail '16 cores · 2.9 GHz' `
            -MiniChartKind Area -MiniChartValues $server.Cpu -MiniChartMaximum 100
        New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind Memory -Label 'MEMORY' `
            -Value $memoryText -Detail 'SQL Server buffer pool' `
            -Progress $memory -StatusValue ($memory * 100) -WarningThreshold 75 -CriticalThreshold 90
        New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind Network -Label 'NETWORK' `
            -Value "$($server.Network[-1]) Mbps" -Detail '10.40.12.21 · 10 GbE' `
            -MiniChartKind Sparkline -MiniChartValues $server.Network
        } else {
            New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind Terminal -Label 'STATUS' `
                -Value 'Unknown' -Detail 'Server data unavailable' -Status Info
        }
    )
    New-BGInfoBackground -Width $Width -Height $Height

    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'PRODUCTION  ·  SQL SERVER 2022' -Accent `
        -FontWeight 700 -FontSize ([int](15 * $scale))
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $server.Name -FontSize ([int](72 * $scale)) `
        -FontWeight 600
    if ($fullest.Value -ge 80) {
        $warning = "1 warning · $($fullest.Key) is $($fullest.Value) % full"
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name "●  $warning" -Status Warning -FontWeight 600
    }
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Role' -Value $server.Role
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Owner' -Value $server.Owner
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Maintenance' -Value $server.Maintenance
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'On call' -Value $server.OnCall

    # The tiles stack in the right column; three panels share the bottom band.
    New-BGInfoVisualCanvas -Region Right -Tile $tiles

    if ($server.Available) {
    $band = @{
        Region    = 'Bottom'
        Height    = [int](300 * $scale)
        NoHistory = $true
    }
    New-BGInfoChart @band -Id 'volumes' -Title 'Volumes used' `
        -Kind ProgressBar -Values @($server.Volumes.Values) `
        -Labels @($server.Volumes.Keys) -Maximum 100 -ValueSuffix ' %' `
        -NoProgressHandles -ShowLatestValue:$false `
        -WarningThreshold 80 -CriticalThreshold 90
    New-BGInfoChart @band -Id 'network' -Title 'Network' -Kind Area `
        -Values $server.Network -ShowGrid -GridLineCount 4 -ValueSuffix ' Mbps'
    $services = $server.Services
    New-BGInfoChart @band -Id 'services' -Title 'Critical services' `
        -Kind Pictorial -Values $services.Running, $services.Stopped `
        -Labels 'Running', 'Stopped' -Palette $look.Ok, $look.Critical `
        -PictorialSymbol Circle -PictorialColumns 12 `
        -Maximum ($services.Running + $services.Stopped) `
        -ShowDataLabels -ShowLatestValue:$false
    }
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory `
    -OutputFileName "server-status-$($Theme.ToLower()).png"
#endregion

<#
    Server status wallpaper: who the server is, how long it has been up,
    and whether disks, services and the network need attention.

    The data block returns plain values; the presentation block only reads
    them. Sample values keep the render reproducible, and each one notes the
    command that supplies it on a real server.
#>
param(
    [ValidateSet('Light', 'Dark')]
    [string] $Theme = 'Dark',
    [int] $Width = 1920,
    [int] $Height = 1080,
    [string] $OutputDirectory = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'Output')
)

Import-Module (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\PowerBGInfo.psd1') -Force

#region Data: your logic goes here
function Get-ServerStatus {
    [pscustomobject] @{
        Available = $true
        Name        = 'SQL-PROD-01'
        Role        = 'Primary replica · AG-FINANCE'
        Owner       = 'Data Platform team'
        Maintenance = 'Sunday 02:00–04:00 UTC'
        OnCall      = 'dba-oncall@contoso.com'
        # (Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).LastBootUpTime
        Uptime      = New-TimeSpan -Days 41 -Hours 6
        # Get-Volume | Where-Object DriveLetter
        Volumes     = [ordered] @{
            'C: System' = 61
            'D: Data'   = 88
            'L: Logs'   = 47
        }
        # Get-Counter '\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time'
        Cpu         = @(12, 28, 19, 44, 31, 38, 27, 23)
        Memory      = @{ UsedGB = 100; TotalGB = 128 }
        # Get-Counter '\Network Interface(*)\Bytes Total/sec'
        Network     = @(180, 210, 260, 240, 310, 420, 380, 350, 300, 312)
        # Get-Service for the services that matter on this server
        Services    = @{ Running = 11; Stopped = 1 }
    }
}

# A slow or broken source must not block logon: time-box it and fall back.
$fallback = [pscustomobject] @{
    Available = $false
    Name = $env:COMPUTERNAME; Role = 'unknown'; Owner = 'unknown'
    Maintenance = 'unknown'; OnCall = 'unknown'; Uptime = [timespan]::Zero
    Volumes = @{ 'C:' = 0 }; Cpu = @(0); Memory = @{ UsedGB = 0; TotalGB = 1 }
    Network = @(0); Services = @{ Running = 0; Stopped = 0 }
}
$source = @{
    Name           = 'Server status'
    TimeoutSeconds = 15
    ScriptBlock    = ${function:Get-ServerStatus}
    Default        = $fallback
}
$server = Invoke-BGInfoDataSource @source
#endregion

$look = New-BGInfoTheme Aurora -Mode $Theme -Scale $scale
$fullest = $server.Volumes.GetEnumerator() |
    Sort-Object Value -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
$memory = $server.Memory.UsedGB / $server.Memory.TotalGB
$uptime = "$($server.Uptime.Days) days $($server.Uptime.Hours) h"
$memoryText = "$($server.Memory.UsedGB) of $($server.Memory.TotalGB) GB"

New-BGInfo -Theme $look -Target File {
    $tile = @{ SurfaceStyle = 'Glass' }
    $tiles = @(
        if ($server.Available) {
        New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind Terminal -Label 'UPTIME' `

        New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind Cpu -Label 'CPU' `
            -Value "$($server.Cpu[-1]) %" -Detail '16 cores · 2.9 GHz' `
            -MiniChartKind Area -MiniChartValues $server.Cpu -MiniChartMaximum 100
        New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind Memory -Label 'MEMORY' `
            -Value $memoryText -Detail 'SQL Server buffer pool' `
            -Progress $memory -StatusValue ($memory * 100) -WarningThreshold 75 -CriticalThreshold 90
        New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind Network -Label 'NETWORK' `
            -Value "$($server.Network[-1]) Mbps" -Detail '10.40.12.21 · 10 GbE' `
            -MiniChartKind Sparkline -MiniChartValues $server.Network
        } else {
            New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind Terminal -Label 'STATUS' `
                -Value 'Unknown' -Detail 'Server data unavailable' -Status Info
        }
    )
    New-BGInfoBackground -Width $Width -Height $Height

    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'PRODUCTION  ·  SQL SERVER 2022' -Accent `
        -FontWeight 700 -FontSize ([int](15 * $scale))
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $server.Name -FontSize ([int](72 * $scale)) `

    if ($fullest.Value -ge 80) {
        $warning = "1 warning · $($fullest.Key) is $($fullest.Value) % full"
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name "●  $warning" -Status Warning -FontWeight 600
    }
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Role' -Value $server.Role
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Owner' -Value $server.Owner
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Maintenance' -Value $server.Maintenance
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'On call' -Value $server.OnCall

    # The tiles stack in the right column; three panels share the bottom band.
    New-BGInfoVisualCanvas -Region Right -Tile $tiles

    if ($server.Available) {
    $band = @{
        Region    = 'Bottom'
        Height    = [int](300 * $scale)
        NoHistory = $true
    }
    New-BGInfoChart @band -Id 'volumes' -Title 'Volumes used' `
        -Kind ProgressBar -Values @($server.Volumes.Values) `

scenarios.title: Admin workstation
scenarios.purpose: Dense privileged-access HUD with the allowed admin path.
scenarios.excerpt:
New-BGInfo -Theme $look -SpaceX $textX -Target File {
    $tile = @{ SurfaceStyle = 'Glass' }
    $tiles = @(
        New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind Cpu -Label 'CPU' -Value "$($paw.Cpu[-1]) %" `
            -Detail '8 cores · Credential Guard on' -MiniChartKind Area -MiniChartValues $paw.Cpu -MiniChartMaximum 100
        New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind Memory -Label 'MEMORY' -Value '9.6 of 32 GB' `
            -Detail 'Hyper-V isolation' -MiniChartKind Bars -MiniChartValues $paw.Memory -MiniChartMaximum 100
        New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind Storage -Label 'SYSTEM DRIVE' -Value "$($paw.SystemFreeGB) GB free" `
            -Detail 'BitLocker · TPM + PIN' -Progress $paw.SystemUsed
        New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind Shield -Label 'DEFENDER' -Value $paw.Defender `
            -Detail ($(if ($paw.Defender -eq 'unknown') { 'Status unavailable' } else { 'Signatures 2 h old' })) -Status $defenderStatus
        New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind OperatingSystem -Label 'PATCH LEVEL' -Value $paw.PatchLevel `
            -Detail 'Ring 0 · pilot' -Status ($(if ($paw.PatchLevel -eq 'unknown') { 'Info' } else { 'Ok' }))
        # Fewer than 30 days left is a warning, fewer than 7 is critical.
        New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile @smartCard -IconKind Domain -Label 'SMART CARD'
        New-BGInfoVisualCanvasTile @tile -IconKind Terminal -Label 'ELEVATION' -Value $paw.Elevation `
            -Detail ($(if ($paw.Available) { 'Approved by S. Ortiz' } else { 'Approval unavailable' })) -Status ($(if ($paw.Available) { 'Warning' } else { 'Info' }))
    )
    New-BGInfoBackground -Width $Width -Height $Height

    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $heading -Status ($(if ($paw.Available) { 'Critical' } else { 'Warning' })) -FontSize ([int](15 * $scale)) -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $paw.Name -FontSize ([int](64 * $scale)) -FontWeight 600
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'No email, no browsing, no personal accounts.' -FontSize ([int](19 * $scale)) -FontWeight 600
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Operator' -Value $paw.Operator
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Domain' -Value $paw.Domain
    if ($paw.Available) {
        New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Reachable' -Value 'Jump host → tier 0 only'
    }

    if ($paw.Available) {
    # The theme puts the canvas rails on its margins; only sizes are set.
    $rail = $tiles | ForEach-Object { $_.Side = 'Left'; $_ }
    New-BGInfoVisualCanvas -Tile $rail -LeftTileWidth $railWidth `
        -TileHeight $tileHeight

    New-BGInfoChart -Id 'signins' -Title 'Privileged sign-ins' -Kind Bar `
        -Values $paw.SignIns -ShowGrid -GridLineCount 3 `
        -ValueSuffix ' today' -NoHistory `
        -Width ([int](560 * $scale)) -Height ([int](270 * $scale)) `
        -Anchor TopRight -OffsetX $look.MarginX -OffsetY $look.MarginY

    $diagram = @{
        Title           = 'Allowed admin path'
        Subtitle        = '2 hops to tier 0'
        Layout          = 'DenseGrouped'
        Scale           = $diagramScale
        NodeDisplayMode = 'Card'
        Width           = $column
        Height          = $diagramHeight
        Anchor          = 'TopRight'
        OffsetX         = $look.MarginX
        OffsetY         = $diagramTop
    }
    New-BGInfoTopology @diagram -TopologyDefinition {

scenarios.source:
<#
    Domain controller health. The question for the administrator at this
    console: is the directory replicating, does this DC hold the roles it
    should, is its clock right, and has anything unusual hit it lately?

    The data block returns plain values; the presentation block only reads
    them. Comments name the command or source that supplies each value.
#>
param(
    [ValidateSet('Light', 'Dark')]
    [string] $Theme = 'Dark',
    [int] $Width = 1920,
    [int] $Height = 1080,
    [string] $OutputDirectory = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'Output')
)

Import-Module (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\PowerBGInfo.psd1') -Force

#region Data: your logic goes here
function Get-DomainControllerHealth {
    $today = Get-Date '2026-10-16'
    [pscustomobject] @{
        Available = $true
        # $env:COMPUTERNAME and (Get-ADDomainController).Site
        Name     = 'DC01'
        Site     = 'AMS-HQ'
        Domain   = 'corp.contoso.com'
        # (Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).Caption
        Os       = 'Windows Server 2025 Datacenter'
        # wbadmin get versions, or your backup product's API
        Backup   = 'System state 02:10 today'
        # Get-ADForest (SchemaMaster, DomainNamingMaster) and
        # Get-ADDomain (PDCEmulator, RIDMaster, InfrastructureMaster)
        Fsmo     = [ordered] @{
            'Schema master'        = 'DC01'
            'Domain naming master' = 'DC01'
            'PDC emulator'         = 'DC01'
            'RID master'           = 'DC02'
            'Infrastructure'       = 'DC02'
        }
        # w32tm /stripchart /computer:time.contoso.com /samples:8 /dataonly
        TimeOffsetMs = 3.4
        TimeHistory  = @(2.1, 2.8, 4.0, 3.1, 2.6, 3.9, 3.2, 3.4)
        TimeSource   = 'time.contoso.com, stratum 2'
        # Get-ADReplicationSite and Get-ADReplicationSiteLink
        Sites    = @(
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Name = 'AMS-HQ'; Servers = 'DC01 · DC02'; Status = 'Healthy'
            }
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Name = 'WAW-BR'; Servers = 'DC03'; Status = 'Healthy'
                Interval = '15 min'
            }
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Name = 'NYC-BR'; Servers = 'DC04'; Status = 'Warning'
                Interval = '3 h late'
            }
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Name = 'LIS-BR'; Servers = 'RODC01'; Status = 'Healthy'
                Interval = '1 h'
            }
        )
        # dcdiag /q, or dcdiag /test:<name> per line
        DiagnosedAt  = 'today 06:00'
        Diagnostics  = @(
            @{ Text = 'Replications'; Status = 'Warning'; Value = 'DC04' }
            @{ Text = 'Connectivity, advertising'; Status = 'Ok'
                Value = 'passed' }
            @{ Text = 'SYSVOL and NetLogons'; Status = 'Ok'; Value = 'passed' }
            @{ Text = 'DNS registration'; Status = 'Ok'; Value = 'passed' }
        )
        # Get-ADReplicationPartnerMetadata -Target $env:COMPUTERNAME
        # and Get-ADReplicationFailure -Target $env:COMPUTERNAME
        Partners = @(
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Partner = 'DC02'; Site = 'AMS-HQ'
                Last = '2 min ago'; Failures = 0; State = 'OK'
            }
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Partner = 'DC03'; Site = 'WAW-BR'
                Last = '11 min ago'; Failures = 0; State = 'OK'
            }
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Partner = 'DC04'; Site = 'NYC-BR'
                Last = '3 h 12 min ago'; Failures = 4; State = 'Warning'
            }
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Partner = 'RODC01'; Site = 'LIS-BR'
                Last = '9 min ago'; Failures = 0; State = 'OK'
            }
        )
        # Failed sign-ins per day: Security log events 4625 and 4771.
        #   Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{
        #       LogName = 'Security'; Id = 4625, 4771
        #       StartTime = (Get-Date).AddDays(-126) } |
        #   Group-Object { $_.TimeCreated.Date }
        Failures = foreach ($day in 0..125) {
            $date = $today.AddDays(-$day)
            $weekend = $date.DayOfWeek -in 'Saturday', 'Sunday'
            $value = if ($weekend) { 2 + $day % 4 } else { 9 + ($day * 7) % 13 }
            # A password-spray attempt three weeks ago stands out.
            if ($day -eq 22) { $value = 96 }
            if ($day -eq 21) { $value = 41 }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Date = $date; Value = $value }
        }
    }
}

$fallback = [pscustomobject] @{
    Available = $false
    Name = $env:COMPUTERNAME; Site = 'unknown'; Domain = 'unknown'
    Os = 'unknown'; Backup = 'unknown'; Fsmo = [ordered] @{}
    TimeOffsetMs = 0; TimeHistory = @(); TimeSource = 'unknown'
    Sites = @(); DiagnosedAt = ''; Diagnostics = @(); Partners = @()
    Failures = @([pscustomobject] @{ Date = (Get-Date).Date; Value = 0 })
}
$source = @{
    Name           = 'Domain controller health'
    TimeoutSeconds = 20
    ScriptBlock    = ${function:Get-DomainControllerHealth}
    Default        = $fallback
}
$dc = Invoke-BGInfoDataSource @source
#endregion

#region Presentation: reads only $dc
$scale = [Math]::Round($Height / 1080, 2)
$look = New-BGInfoTheme Graphite -Mode $Theme -Scale $scale
$failing = @($dc.Partners | Where-Object State -NE 'OK')
$held = @($dc.Fsmo.GetEnumerator() | Where-Object Value -EQ $dc.Name)

New-BGInfo -Theme $look -Target File {
    New-BGInfoBackground -Width $Width -Height $Height

    New-BGInfoLabel -Name "DOMAIN CONTROLLER  ·  $($dc.Domain.ToUpper())" `
        -Accent -FontSize ([int](15 * $scale)) -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $dc.Name -FontSize ([int](72 * $scale)) `
        -FontWeight 600
    if ($dc.Partners.Count -eq 0) {
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name '●  Replication data unavailable' -Status Info `
            -FontWeight 600
    } elseif ($failing.Count -gt 0) {
        $partner = $failing[0]
        $text = "Replication from $($partner.Partner) last succeeded " +
            $partner.Last
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name "●  $text" -Status Warning -FontWeight 600
    } else {
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name '●  Replicating with every partner' -Status Ok `
            -FontWeight 600
    }
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Site' -Value $dc.Site

    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'System' -Value $dc.Os
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Backup' -Value $dc.Backup

    # Right column: who holds each FSMO role, and how far the clock drifts.
    $roles = foreach ($role in $dc.Fsmo.GetEnumerator()) {
        @{ Text = $role.Key; Value = $role.Value; Status = 'Ok' }
    }
    if ($dc.Available) {
        New-BGInfoList -Region Right -Title 'FSMO roles' `
            -Note "$($held.Count) of 5 here" -Item $roles
        New-BGInfoMetric -Region Right -Label 'Time offset' `
            -Value $dc.TimeOffsetMs -Unit 'ms' -Caption $dc.TimeSource `
            -History $dc.TimeHistory -WarningThreshold 100 -CriticalThreshold 1000 `
            -Height ([int](150 * $scale))
    }

    # Center: every inbound partner, warnings first.
    if ($dc.Partners.Count -gt 0) {
        $dc.Partners | Sort-Object { $_.State -eq 'OK' } |
            New-BGInfoTable -Region Center -Title 'Inbound replication' `
                -Note "$($dc.Partners.Count) partners" -StatusColumn State
    }

    # Bottom band: the site links, dcdiag and the failed sign-in history.
    $band = @{ Region = 'Bottom'; Height = [int](290 * $scale) }
    if ($dc.Sites.Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoTopology @band -Title 'Site links' -Subtitle 'from AMS-HQ' `
            -Layout HubAndSpoke -NodeDisplayMode Card `
            -Width ([int](600 * $scale)) -TopologyDefinition {
            foreach ($site in $dc.Sites) {
                New-BGInfoTopologyNode -Id $site.Name -Label $site.Name `
                    -Subtitle $site.Servers -Kind Location -Status $site.Status
            }
            foreach ($site in $dc.Sites | Where-Object Interval) {
                New-BGInfoTopologyEdge -SourceNodeId $dc.Site `
                    -TargetNodeId $site.Name -Label $site.Interval `
                    -Kind Replication -Status $site.Status
            }
        }
    }
    if ($dc.Available) {
        New-BGInfoList @band -Title 'dcdiag' -Note $dc.DiagnosedAt `
            -Item $dc.Diagnostics
        $dc.Failures | New-BGInfoCalendarHeatmap @band -Title 'Failed sign-ins' `
            -Note 'events 4625 and 4771' -Width ([int](660 * $scale))
    }
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory `
    -OutputFileName "domain-controller-$($Theme.ToLower()).png"
#endregion

<#

#>
param(

    [string] $Theme = 'Dark',
    [int] $Width = 1920,

Import-Module (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\PowerBGInfo.psd1') -Force

#region Data: your logic goes here
function Get-HyperVHostData {
    # Get-VM returns these properties (MemoryAssigned, ProcessorCount and
    # CPUUsage); the workload tag comes from the VM notes or your CMDB.
    # The sample keeps them as CSV to stay short.
    $vms = @'
Name,Workload,vCPU,MemoryGB,Cpu
SQL-PROD-01,Databases,16,128,71
SQL-PROD-02,Databases,16,96,34
SQL-RPT-01,Databases,8,48,12
ERP-APP-01,ERP,12,64,38
ERP-APP-02,ERP,12,64,29
ERP-BATCH-01,ERP,8,32,55
VDI-POOL-A,Desktops,48,96,41
VDI-POOL-B,Desktops,24,48,18
WEB-01,Web,4,16,22
WEB-02,Web,4,16,19
WEB-03,Web,4,16,9
FS-01,Infrastructure,4,32,6
MON-01,Infrastructure,4,24,14
DC02,Infrastructure,2,8,3
'@ | ConvertFrom-Csv | ForEach-Object {
        [pscustomobject] @{
            Name = $_.Name; Workload = $_.Workload; vCPU = [int] $_.vCPU
            MemoryGB = [int] $_.MemoryGB; Cpu = [int] $_.Cpu; State = 'Running'
        }
    }

    [pscustomobject] @{
        Available = $true
        Name     = 'HV-AMS-07'
        # Get-Cluster and Get-ClusterNode
        Cluster  = 'HVC-AMS-01 · node 3 of 6'
        Hardware = '2 × Xeon Gold 6448Y · 64 cores'
        Version  = 'Windows Server 2025 Datacenter'
        # Get-Counter '\Hyper-V Hypervisor Logical Processor(_Total)\
        #     % Total Run Time' sampled every 5 minutes
        Cpu      = @(38, 41, 52, 47, 44, 49, 46)
        # (Get-VMHost).MemoryCapacity and the sum of MemoryAssigned
        MemoryGB = [int] ($vms | Measure-Object -Property MemoryGB -Sum).Sum
        # The cluster keeps one node's worth of memory free for failover.
        ReserveGB = 64
        TotalGB  = 768
        # Get-ClusterSharedVolume | Select-Object -ExpandProperty
        #     SharedVolumeInfo | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Partition
        Storage  = @{ Name = 'CSV-02'; UsedPercent = 68; FreeTB = 6.1 }
        Vms      = $vms
        # Get-ClusterGroup | Where-Object OwnerNode -NE $env:COMPUTERNAME,
        # or the Failover Clustering event log, event 5143 and 1641
        Moves    = @(
            [pscustomobject] @{ Time = '09:12'; VM = 'ERP-BATCH-01'
                Move = 'from HV-AMS-04'; Result = 'OK' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Time = '08:47'; VM = 'WEB-03'
                Move = 'from HV-AMS-02'; Result = 'OK' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Time = '02:05'; VM = 'VDI-POOL-B'
                Move = 'to HV-AMS-05'; Result = 'Failed' }
        )
        # Memory assigned on every node: Get-ClusterNode | ForEach-Object {
        #     Get-VM -ComputerName $_.Name | Measure-Object MemoryAssigned }
        Nodes       = [ordered] @{
            'HV-AMS-04' = 71; 'HV-AMS-05' = 64; 'HV-AMS-07' = 82
            'HV-AMS-08' = 91; 'HV-AMS-09' = 58; 'HV-AMS-10' = 47
        }
        # Get-VM | Get-VMSnapshot | Where-Object CreationTime -LT
        #     (Get-Date).AddDays(-7)
        Checkpoints = @(
            @{ Text = 'ERP-APP-02 · before CU 14'; Status = 'Warning'
                Value = '12 days' }
            @{ Text = 'WEB-02 · config test'; Status = 'Warning'
                Value = '9 days' }
        )
    }
}

$fallback = [pscustomobject] @{
    Available = $false
    Name = $env:COMPUTERNAME; Cluster = 'unknown'; Hardware = 'unknown'
    Version = 'unknown'; Cpu = @(0); MemoryGB = 0; TotalGB = 1; ReserveGB = 0
    Storage = @{ Name = 'CSV'; UsedPercent = 0; FreeTB = 0 }
    Vms = @([pscustomobject] @{ Name = 'unknown'; Workload = ''
            vCPU = 0; MemoryGB = 1; Cpu = 0; State = 'Unknown' })
    Moves = @(); Checkpoints = @(); Nodes = [ordered] @{ 'unknown' = 0 }
}
$source = @{
    Name           = 'Hyper-V host'
    TimeoutSeconds = 20
    ScriptBlock    = ${function:Get-HyperVHostData}
    Default        = $fallback
}
$hv = Invoke-BGInfoDataSource @source
#endregion

#region Presentation: reads only $hv
$scale = [Math]::Round($Height / 1080, 2)
$look = New-BGInfoTheme Corporate -Mode $Theme -Scale $scale
$memory = [Math]::Round(100 * $hv.MemoryGB / $hv.TotalGB)
$running = @($hv.Vms | Where-Object State -EQ 'Running').Count
$vcpu = ($hv.Vms | Measure-Object vCPU -Sum).Sum
$free = $hv.TotalGB - $hv.MemoryGB - $hv.ReserveGB

New-BGInfo -Theme $look -Target File {
    New-BGInfoBackground -Width $Width -Height $Height -Pattern Grid `
        -PatternSpacing ([int](56 * $scale))
    # A wider right column for the tables; the treemap may fill the center.
    New-BGInfoLayout -ColumnWidth ([int](520 * $scale)) `
        -MaximumPanelHeight ([int](640 * $scale))

    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'HYPER-V HOST  ·  PRODUCTION CLUSTER' -Accent `
        -FontSize ([int](15 * $scale)) -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $hv.Name -FontSize ([int](72 * $scale)) `
        -FontWeight 600
    $capacity = if ($hv.Available) {
        "Room for $free GB of VMs before failover reserve"
    } else { 'Host capacity unavailable' }
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $capacity `
        -FontSize ([int](19 * $scale)) -FontWeight 600
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Cluster' -Value $hv.Cluster
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Hardware' -Value $hv.Hardware
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'System' -Value $hv.Version

    # Top band: four host metrics beside the text. Above 80 % memory or
    # 75 % storage the card turns amber; above 90 % it turns red.
    if ($hv.Available) {
        $card = @{ Region = 'Top'; Height = [int](170 * $scale) }
        New-BGInfoMetric @card -Label 'CPU' -Value $hv.Cpu[-1] -Unit '%' `
            -Caption '64 logical cores' -History $hv.Cpu -HistoryMaximum 100 `
            -WarningThreshold 70 -CriticalThreshold 85
        New-BGInfoMetric @card -Label 'Memory' -Value $memory -Unit '%' `
            -Caption "$($hv.MemoryGB) of $($hv.TotalGB) GB assigned" `
            -WarningThreshold 80 -CriticalThreshold 90
        New-BGInfoMetric @card -Label $hv.Storage.Name -Unit '%' `
            -Value $hv.Storage.UsedPercent `
            -Caption "$($hv.Storage.FreeTB) TB free" `
            -WarningThreshold 75 -CriticalThreshold 90
        New-BGInfoMetric @card -Label 'VMs running' -Value $running `
            -Caption "$vcpu vCPU on 64 cores"

        # Center: where the memory goes, grouped by workload. The color is the
        # VM's CPU: amber from 60 %, red from 85 %.
        $hv.Vms | New-BGInfoTreemap -Region Center -Title 'Memory by VM' `
            -Note 'size: memory · color: CPU' -ValueProperty MemoryGB `
            -GroupProperty Workload -ValueSuffix ' GB' -ColorProperty Cpu `
            -WarningThreshold 60 -CriticalThreshold 85

        # Right column: cluster memory by node, today's live migrations and the
        # checkpoints left behind. Each node keeps its label and palette color.
        New-BGInfoChart -Region Right -Id 'nodes' -Title 'Cluster memory' `
            -Kind HorizontalBar -Values @($hv.Nodes.Values) `
            -Labels @($hv.Nodes.Keys) `
            -Palette @($look.Accent, $look.SecondaryAccent, $look.Ok, `
                $look.Warning, $look.Critical, $look.Info) `
            -Maximum 100 -ValueSuffix ' %' -NoHistory `
            -Height ([int](250 * $scale))
        $hv.Moves | New-BGInfoTable -Region Right -Title 'Live migrations' `
            -Note 'today' -Property Time, VM, Result -StatusColumn Result
        New-BGInfoList -Region Right -Title 'Old checkpoints' `
            -Note 'older than 7 days' -Item $hv.Checkpoints
    }
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory `
    -OutputFileName "hyperv-host-$($Theme.ToLower()).png"
#endregion

Metric cards with status bars and a sparkline
Horizontal cluster memory bars with node labels and a palette

<#
    Branch office PC. The question for the person at this desk: where am I
    connected, is the link to head office up, and how do I get help?

    The data block returns plain values; the presentation block only reads
    them. Comments name the command or source that supplies each value.
#>
param(
    [ValidateSet('Light', 'Dark')]
    [string] $Theme = 'Light',
    [int] $Width = 1920,
    [int] $Height = 1080,
    [string] $OutputDirectory = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'Output')
)

Import-Module (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\PowerBGInfo.psd1') -Force

#region Data: your logic goes here
function Get-BranchOfficeData {
    [pscustomobject] @{
        # (Get-ADComputer $env:COMPUTERNAME -Properties Location).Location,
        # or a subnet-to-site table: (Get-NetIPAddress).IPAddress
        Site     = 'Warsaw · Mokotów'
        SiteCode = 'WAW-02'
        Computer = 'WAW02-PC-014'
        Printer  = 'WAW02-PRN-01, 2nd floor'
        Contact  = 'Office manager, ext. 2210'
        Wifi     = 'CONTOSO-STAFF'
        # Test-NetConnection to each device, or your SD-WAN controller's
        # API. Everything here hangs off the office switch.
        Switch   = @{ Label = 'Switch'; Detail = '1 GbE' }
        Links    = @(
            [pscustomobject] @{ Id = 'pc'; Label = 'This PC'
                Detail = '10.62.14.37'; Kind = 'Endpoint'; Status = 'Healthy' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Id = 'prn'; Label = 'Printer'
                Detail = '2nd floor'; Kind = 'Endpoint'; Status = 'Healthy' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Id = 'edge'; Label = 'SD-WAN'
                Detail = 'MPLS · 18 ms'; Kind = 'Gateway'; Status = 'Healthy' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Id = 'lte'; Label = 'LTE'
                Detail = 'standby'; Kind = 'Gateway'
                Status = 'Disabled' }
        )
        Backup   = 'LTE backup ready'
        # The branch calendar, or opening hours from your intranet
        Hours    = @(
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Day = 'Mon–Fri'; Office = '08:00–18:00'; IT = '07:00–19:00' }
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Day = 'Saturday'; Office = '09:00–13:00'; IT = 'on call' }
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Day = 'Sunday'; Office = 'closed'; IT = 'on call' }
        )
        HelpUrl  = 'https://help.contoso.com/new?site=WAW-02'
    }
}

$fallback = [pscustomobject] @{
    Site = 'Contoso'; SiteCode = 'unknown'; Computer = $env:COMPUTERNAME
    Printer = 'unknown'; Contact = 'Service desk, ext. 4357'
    Wifi = 'unknown'
    Switch = @{ Label = 'Switch'; Detail = '' }; Links = @(); Backup = ''
    Hours = @()
    HelpUrl = 'https://help.contoso.com/new'
}
$source = @{
    Name           = 'Branch office data'
    TimeoutSeconds = 15
    ScriptBlock    = ${function:Get-BranchOfficeData}
    Default        = $fallback
}
$branch = Invoke-BGInfoDataSource @source
#endregion

#region Presentation: reads only $branch
$scale = [Math]::Round($Height / 1080, 2)
$dark = $Theme -eq 'Dark'
# Aurora with a green accent and dots: calm, and clearly not a server.
$accent = if ($dark) { '#4ADE80' } else { '#15803D' }
$dots = if ($dark) { '#FFFFFF10' } else { '#14532D14' }
$look = New-BGInfoTheme Aurora -Mode $Theme -Scale $scale -Accent $accent
$down = @($branch.Links | Where-Object Status -EQ 'Critical')
# The diagram is small for its panel; a higher scale draws it larger.
$diagramScale = 2

New-BGInfo -Theme $look -Target File {
    New-BGInfoBackground -Width $Width -Height $Height -Pattern Dots `
        -PatternColor $dots -PatternSpacing ([int](28 * $scale))
    # The connection diagram fills the space under the text.
    New-BGInfoLayout -MaximumPanelHeight ([int](640 * $scale))

    New-BGInfoLabel -Name "CONTOSO BRANCH  ·  $($branch.SiteCode)" -Accent `
        -FontSize ([int](15 * $scale)) -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $branch.Site -FontSize ([int](72 * $scale)) `
        -FontWeight 600
    if ($branch.Links.Count -eq 0) {
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name '●  Connectivity unavailable' -Status Info `
            -FontWeight 600
    } elseif ($down.Count -eq 0) {
        $text = "Connected to head office · $($branch.Backup)"
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name "●  $text" -Status Ok -FontWeight 600
    } else {
        $text = "$($down[0].Label) is not reachable, call ext. 4357"
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name "●  $text" -Status Critical -FontWeight 600
    }
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'This PC' -Value $branch.Computer
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Printer' -Value $branch.Printer
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Wi-Fi' -Value $branch.Wifi
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Local help' -Value $branch.Contact

    # Right column: a ticket from the phone, and when someone is here.
    New-BGInfoQRCode -Region Right -Url $branch.HelpUrl `
        -Title 'Scan for IT help' -Caption 'help.contoso.com' `
        -Note 'opens a ticket' -Height ([int](330 * $scale))
    if ($branch.Hours.Count -gt 0) {
        $branch.Hours | New-BGInfoTable -Region Right -Title 'Opening hours' `
            -Property Day, Office, @{ Name = 'IT desk'
                Expression = { $_.IT } }
    }

    # Center: everything this desk depends on, around the office switch.
    if ($branch.Links.Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoTopology -Region Center -Height 0 `
            -Title 'Your connection' -Subtitle 'checked 2 min ago' `
            -Layout HubAndSpoke -NodeDisplayMode Card -Scale $diagramScale `
            -TopologyDefinition {
            New-BGInfoTopologyNode -Id 'sw' -Label $branch.Switch.Label `
                -Subtitle $branch.Switch.Detail -Kind Network -Status Healthy
            foreach ($device in $branch.Links) {
                New-BGInfoTopologyNode -Id $device.Id -Label $device.Label `
                    -Subtitle $device.Detail -Kind $device.Kind `
                    -Status $device.Status
            }
            foreach ($device in $branch.Links) {
                New-BGInfoTopologyEdge -SourceNodeId 'sw' `
                    -TargetNodeId $device.Id `
                    -Kind Connectivity -Status $device.Status
            }
        }
    }
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory `
    -OutputFileName "branch-office-$($Theme.ToLower()).png"
#endregion

    # Microsoft Graph: GET /users/{room}/calendarView for today, for this

    function Booking($room, $from, $to) {

        [pscustomobject] @{

    [pscustomobject] @{

        Seats    = '10 seats · video bar · whiteboard'
        Book     = 'Outlook or Teams, room "Oslo 4.12"'

scenarios.source:
<#
    Build agent or CI runner. The question for the engineer who remotes in:
    is this agent busy or broken, what ran last, and is there disk left?

    The data block returns plain values; the presentation block only reads
    them. Comments name the command or source that supplies each value.
#>
param(
    [ValidateSet('Light', 'Dark')]
    [string] $Theme = 'Dark',
    [int] $Width = 1920,
    [int] $Height = 1080,
    [string] $OutputDirectory = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'Output')
)

Import-Module (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\PowerBGInfo.psd1') -Force

#region Data: your logic goes here
function Get-BuildAgentData {
    [pscustomobject] @{
        Name      = 'BLD-WIN-04'
        Available = $true
        Pool      = 'WIN-BUILD-2025'
        # .agent and .credentials in the agent folder, or the pool API:
        # GET {org}/_apis/distributedtask/pools/{id}/agents
        #     ?includeAssignedRequest=true
        Agent     = '4.255.0 · runs as a service'
        Toolchain = 'VS 2022 17.14 · .NET 10 SDK · Node 22'
        Job       = 'payments-api CI #48213'
        Stage     = 'Test'
        Waiting   = 3
        # Get-Volume -DriveLetter C, D | Select-Object DriveLetter,
        #     SizeRemaining, Size
        Disks     = @(
            [pscustomobject] @{ Name = 'D: work'; FreeGB = 182; SizeGB = 512 }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Name = 'C: system'; FreeGB = 34; SizeGB = 256 }
        )
        # GET {org}/{project}/_apis/build/builds
        #     ?$top=5&queryOrder=finishTimeDescending
        Builds    = @(
            [pscustomobject] @{ Pipeline = 'payments-api CI'; Branch = 'main'
                Result = 'Running'; Time = '6 min' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Pipeline = 'web-portal PR 1182'
                Branch = 'feature/sso'; Result = 'Passed'; Time = '14 min' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Pipeline = 'mobile-sdk nightly'; Branch = 'main'
                Result = 'Failed'; Time = '3 min' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Pipeline = 'infra-templates'
                Branch = 'release/26.10'; Result = 'Passed'; Time = '8 min' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Pipeline = 'payments-api CI'; Branch = 'main'
                Result = 'Passed'; Time = '11 min' }
        )
        # The stages of the running pipeline, from its YAML.
        Stages    = 'Checkout', 'Restore', 'Build', 'Test', 'Sign', 'Publish'
    }
}

$fallback = [pscustomobject] @{
    Name = $env:COMPUTERNAME; Available = $false
    Pool = 'unknown'; Agent = 'unknown'; Toolchain = 'unknown'
    Job = 'unavailable'; Stage = ''; Waiting = 0
    Disks = @(); Builds = @(); Stages = @()
}
$source = @{
    Name           = 'Build agent data'
    TimeoutSeconds = 15
    ScriptBlock    = ${function:Get-BuildAgentData}
    Default        = $fallback
}
$agent = Invoke-BGInfoDataSource @source
#endregion

#region Presentation: reads only $agent
$scale = [Math]::Round($Height / 1080, 2)
$dark = $Theme -eq 'Dark'
# Graphite with an emerald accent and dots: the terminal look of a runner.
$accent = if ($dark) { '#34D399' } else { '#047857' }
$dots = if ($dark) { '#FFFFFF0E' } else { '#0F172A12' }
$look = New-BGInfoTheme Graphite -Mode $Theme -Scale $scale -Accent $accent
# The pipeline as a Mermaid flow: done stages, the running one, the rest.
$at = [array]::IndexOf([string[]] $agent.Stages, $agent.Stage)
$nodes = for ($i = 0; $i -lt $agent.Stages.Count; $i++) {
    "S$i[$($agent.Stages[$i])]"
}
$done = if ($at -gt 0) { (0..($at - 1) | ForEach-Object { "S$_" }) -join ',' }
$fill = if ($dark) {
    @{
        Done = 'fill:#064E3B,stroke:#34D399'
        Now  = 'fill:#047857,stroke:#6EE7B7'
    }
} else {
    @{
        Done = 'fill:#D1FAE5,stroke:#059669'
        Now  = 'fill:#6EE7B7,stroke:#047857'
    }
}
$flow = @(
    'flowchart LR'
    '    ' + ($nodes -join ' --> ')
    "    classDef done $($fill.Done)"
    "    classDef now $($fill.Now),stroke-width:3px"
    if ($at -gt 0) { "    class $done done" }
    if ($at -ge 0) { "    class S$at now" }
) -join "`n"

New-BGInfo -Theme $look -Target File {
    New-BGInfoBackground -Width $Width -Height $Height -Pattern Dots `
        -PatternColor $dots -PatternSpacing ([int](24 * $scale))

    New-BGInfoLabel -Name "BUILD AGENT  ·  POOL $($agent.Pool)" -Accent `
        -FontSize ([int](15 * $scale)) -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $agent.Name -FontSize ([int](72 * $scale)) `
        -FontWeight 600
    if ($agent.Available) {
        $activity = if ($at -ge 0) { "▶  Running $($agent.Job)" } else {
            "$($agent.Job) · no active stage"
        }
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name $activity -Accent `
            -FontWeight 600
    } else {
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'Build data unavailable' -Status Info `
            -FontWeight 600
    }
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Agent' -Value $agent.Agent
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Toolchain' -Value $agent.Toolchain
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Clean-up' -Value 'Sunday 03:00, keeps 3 days'

    # Right column: the queue, then free space. Free space is worse when
    # low: amber below 100 GB on the work drive, red below 50 GB.
    if ($agent.Available) {
        New-BGInfoMetric -Region Right -Label 'Waiting in the pool' `
            -Value $agent.Waiting -Unit 'jobs' -Caption '4 agents online' `
            -Height ([int](150 * $scale))
    }
    foreach ($disk in $agent.Disks) {
        $limits = if ($disk.Name -like 'D:*') { 100, 50 } else { 40, 20 }
        New-BGInfoMetric -Region Right -Label "$($disk.Name) free" `
            -Value $disk.FreeGB -Unit 'GB' -Caption "of $($disk.SizeGB) GB" `
            -WarningThreshold $limits[0] -CriticalThreshold $limits[1] `
            -ThresholdDirection Below -Height ([int](150 * $scale))
    }

    # Center: what ran here last. Bottom band: where the current job is.
    if ($agent.Available) {
        if ($agent.Builds.Count -gt 0) {
            $agent.Builds | New-BGInfoTable -Region Center -Title 'Last builds' `
                -Note 'on this agent' -StatusColumn Result -StatusMap @{ Running = 'Info' }
        }
        if ($agent.Stages.Count -gt 0) {
            $stageNote = if ($at -ge 0) {
                "stage $($at + 1) of $($agent.Stages.Count)"
            } else { 'No active stage' }
            New-BGInfoMermaid -Region Bottom -Height ([int](200 * $scale)) `
                -Title $agent.Job -Note $stageNote `
                -Definition $flow
        }
    }
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory `
    -OutputFileName "build-agent-$($Theme.ToLower()).png"
#endregion
features: Mermaid pipeline with classDef styling for the current stage
Status table of recent builds
Metric cards for free disk space

    }

        # example the deadline in Get-WUSettings or your RMM's schedule.
        Now       = Get-Date '2026-10-16 18:45'
        RestartAt = Get-Date '2026-10-16 21:00'
        GraceMin  = 240
        Computer  = 'FIN-LT-0457'
        Ring      = 'Ring 2'
        # Get-WindowsUpdate (PSWindowsUpdate), or the WSUS / Intune report
        Updates   = '2026-10 cumulative update · .NET 10.0.3'
        # The update rings: when each ring installs and when it restarts.
        # Windows Update for Business deferrals and deadlines, or the
        # change calendar for servers.
        Windows   = @(
            Window 'Ring 0 · IT' 0 19 12 'Installed'
            Window 'Ring 1 · pilot' 1 9 22 'Installed'

        Rings     = [ordered] @{
            'Ring 0' = 100; 'Ring 1' = 97; 'Ring 2' = 41; 'Ring 3' = 0

            -Kind Gauge -Values $minutes -Maximum $patch.GraceMin `

<#
    Production or test. The question for the administrator who just signed
    in over Remote Desktop: which environment is this, and what am I allowed
    to change here? The whole wallpaper takes the environment's colour, so a
    production server never looks like its test twin.

    The data block returns plain values; the presentation block only reads
    them. Comments name the command or source that supplies each value.
#>
param(
    [ValidateSet('Light', 'Dark')]
    [string] $Theme = 'Dark',
    [int] $Width = 1920,
    [int] $Height = 1080,
    [string] $OutputDirectory = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'Output'),
    # Render the same layout for another environment to compare them.
    [ValidateSet('Production', 'Acceptance', 'Test', 'Development')]
    [string] $Environment = 'Production'
)

Import-Module (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\PowerBGInfo.psd1') -Force

#region Data: your logic goes here
function Get-EnvironmentInfo {
    param([string] $Environment)
    $today = Get-Date '2026-10-16 09:40'
    # One machine per environment for the same service. In practice read the
    # environment from a CMDB, a registry value set at build time, or a tag:
    #   (Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Contoso\Server').Environment
    #   (Invoke-RestMethod -Headers @{ Metadata = 'true' } -Uri
    #       'http://169.254.169.254/metadata/instance?api-version=2021-02-01'
    #   ).compute.tagsList
    $hosts = [ordered] @{
        Production  = 'PAY-PRD-07'
        Acceptance  = 'PAY-UAT-02'
        Test        = 'PAY-TST-04'
        Development = 'PAY-DEV-01'
    }
    [pscustomobject] @{
        Available   = $true
        Environment = $Environment
        Name        = $hosts[$Environment]
        Service     = 'Payments API'
        Company     = 'Contoso Finance'
        # (Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).Caption
        Os          = 'Windows Server 2025 Standard'
        # Get-WebSite, or the role your build pipeline records
        Role        = 'IIS application server, pool PaymentsApi'
        Owner       = 'Payments Platform team'
        Data        = 'Confidential: cardholder data in scope'
        # Your change policy, per environment
        Policy      = switch ($Environment) {
            'Production' { 'Every change needs an approved CAB ticket' }
            'Acceptance' { 'Changes need sign-off from the release manager' }
            'Test' { 'Free to change; reset from image every Monday' }
            'Development' { 'Free to change; nothing here is backed up' }
        }
        Link        = 'https://change.contoso.com/policy/payments'
        # Your change calendar API, for example ServiceNow change_request:
        # one lane per change window, with its approval state.
        Windows     = @(
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Lane = 'Monthly patching'; Category = 'Done'
                Start = $today.Date.AddDays(-1).AddHours(22)
                End = $today.Date.AddDays(-1).AddHours(25)
            }
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Lane = 'Release 4.12'; Category = 'Approved'
                Start = $today.Date.AddDays(1).AddHours(21)
                End = $today.Date.AddDays(1).AddHours(23)
            }
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Lane = 'SQL index rebuild'; Category = 'Approved'
                Start = $today.Date.AddDays(2).AddHours(1)
                End = $today.Date.AddDays(2).AddHours(4)
            }
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Lane = 'Firewall rule change'; Category = 'Awaiting approval'
                Start = $today.Date.AddDays(3).AddHours(19)
                End = $today.Date.AddDays(3).AddHours(21)
            }
        )
        Now         = $today
        # The same service in every environment, from your CMDB
        Siblings    = foreach ($entry in $hosts.GetEnumerator()) {
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Environment = $entry.Key
                Host        = $entry.Value
                Version     = switch ($entry.Key) {
                    'Production' { '4.11.2' } 'Acceptance' { '4.12 RC2' }
                    'Test' { '4.12 RC3' } 'Development' { '4.13 dev' }
                }
            }
        }
        # Get-HotFix | Sort-Object InstalledOn | Select-Object -Last 1, plus
        # the last deployment from your release pipeline
        LastChange  = 'Release 4.11.2, 3 days ago, CHG0042117'
    }
}

$fallback = [pscustomobject] @{
    Available = $false; Environment = $Environment; Name = $env:COMPUTERNAME
    Service = 'unknown'; Company = ''; Os = 'unknown'; Role = 'unknown'
    Owner = 'unknown'; Data = 'unknown'
    Policy = 'Environment unknown: treat as production'
    Link = ''; Windows = @(); Now = Get-Date; Siblings = @()
    LastChange = 'unknown'
}
$source = @{
    Name           = 'Environment'
    TimeoutSeconds = 10
    ScriptBlock    = ${function:Get-EnvironmentInfo}
    ArgumentList   = @($Environment)

}
$envInfo = Invoke-BGInfoDataSource @source

#region Presentation: reads only $envInfo
$scale = [Math]::Round($Height / 1080, 2)
# One colour per environment drives the accent, the glows and the headline.
$colors = @{
    Production  = @{
        Accent = '#EF4444'; Glow = '#EF444455'; GlowLight = '#FCA5A588'
        Status = 'Critical'
    }
    Acceptance  = @{
        Accent = '#F59E0B'; Glow = '#F59E0B4D'; GlowLight = '#FCD34D88'

    }
    Test        = @{
        Accent = '#22C55E'; Glow = '#22C55E44'; GlowLight = '#86EFAC88'
        Status = 'Ok'
    }
    Development = @{
        Accent = '#3B82F6'; Glow = '#3B82F644'; GlowLight = '#93C5FD88'

    }
}
$color = $colors[$envInfo.Environment]
$glow = if ($Theme -eq 'Dark') { $color.Glow } else { $color.GlowLight }

New-BGInfo -Theme $look -Target File {

    New-BGInfoBackground -Width $Width -Height $Height -GradientAngle 150 `

        -FontWeight 600
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name "●  $($envInfo.Policy)" -Status $color.Status `
        -FontWeight 600

    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'System' -Value $envInfo.Os
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Owner' -Value $envInfo.Owner
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Data' -Value $envInfo.Data

    # Right column: where to read the policy, and the same service elsewhere.
    if ($envInfo.Link) {
        $link = [uri] $envInfo.Link
        New-BGInfoQRCode -Region Right -Text $envInfo.Link `
            -Title 'Change policy' `
            -Caption "$($link.Host)$($link.AbsolutePath)" `
            -Height ([int](400 * $scale))
    }
    if (@($envInfo.Siblings).Count -gt 0) {
        # Each environment in its own colour; the one you are on says so.
        $environments = foreach ($sibling in $envInfo.Siblings) {

                Value  = "$($sibling.Host)  ·  $($sibling.Version)"
                Status = $colors[$sibling.Environment].Status
            }
        }
        New-BGInfoList -Region Right -Title 'Same service' -Item $environments

    if (@($envInfo.Windows).Count -gt 0) {
        $states = @{
            'Done'              = $look.Ok
            'Approved'          = $look.Muted
            'Awaiting approval' = $look.Warning
        }
        $windows = $envInfo.Windows | Select-Object *, @{
            Name = 'Color'; Expression = { "$($states[$_.Category].ToHex())" }
        }
        New-BGInfoTimeline -Region Bottom -Title 'Change windows' `
            -Note 'this week, local time' -Item $windows -Now $envInfo.Now `
            -Height ([int](300 * $scale))
    }
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory `
    -OutputFileName "environment-marker-$($Theme.ToLower()).png"
#endregion

QR code to the change policy

scenarios.excerpt:
New-BGInfo -Theme $look -Target File {
    New-BGInfoBackground -Width $Width -Height $Height -Pattern Dots `
        -PatternSpacing ([int](28 * $scale))
    # A wide right column so the session table keeps every column readable.
    New-BGInfoLayout -ColumnWidth ([int](620 * $scale))

    New-BGInfoLabel -Name "RDS SESSION HOST  ·  $($rds.Collection.ToUpper())" `
        -Accent -FontSize ([int](15 * $scale)) -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $rds.Name -FontSize ([int](72 * $scale)) `
        -FontWeight 600
    switch ($rds.Accepting) {
        'Yes' {
            $broker = $rds.Broker.Split('.')[0].ToUpper()
            New-BGInfoLabel -Name "●  Accepting new sessions from $broker" `
                -Status Ok -FontWeight 600
        }
        'unknown' {
            New-BGInfoLabel -Name '●  Broker state unavailable' -Status Info `
                -FontWeight 600
        }
        default {
            New-BGInfoLabel -Name '●  Drain mode: no new sessions' `
                -Status Warning -FontWeight 600
        }
    }
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Collection' `
        -Value "$($rds.Collection), $($rds.Hosts) hosts"
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Broker' -Value $rds.Broker
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'System' -Value $rds.Os
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Profiles' -Value "FSLogix on $($rds.ProfileShare)"
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Restart' -Value $rds.Restart

    # Right column: who is on the host, heaviest first, then whose profile
    # container is close to its cap (amber from 80 %, red from 90 %).
    if (@($rds.Sessions).Count -gt 0) {
        $rds.Sessions | Sort-Object Cpu -Descending |
            Select-Object User, State, Idle,
                @{ Name = 'CPU'; Expression = { "$($_.Cpu) %" } },
                @{ Name = 'Memory'; Expression = { "$($_.MemoryGB) GB" } } |
            New-BGInfoTable -Region Right -Title 'Who is on it' `
                -Note "$(@($rds.Sessions).Count) of $sessions by CPU" `
                -StatusColumn State -StatusMap @{ Active = 'Ok'; Disconnected = 'Warning' }
    }
    if ($rds.Containers.Count -gt 0) {
        $percent = foreach ($size in $rds.Containers.Values) {
            [Math]::Round(100 * $size / $rds.ProfileCapGB)
        }
        $title = 'Largest FSLogix containers  ·  ' +
            "cap $($rds.ProfileCapGB) GB"
        New-BGInfoChart -Region Right -Id 'containers' -Title $title `
            -Kind ProgressBar -Values $percent -Labels @($rds.Containers.Keys) `
            -Maximum 100 -ValueSuffix ' %' -NoHistory -NoProgressHandles `
            -ShowLatestValue:$false -ShowDataLabels `
            -WarningThreshold 80 -CriticalThreshold 90
    }

    # Center, under the text: how long sign-ins took over two weeks. A spike
    # usually means a GPO, profile or antivirus change.
    if (@($rds.Logon).Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoChart -Region Center -Id 'logon' `
            -Title 'Average logon  ·  last 14 days' `
            -Kind Bar -Values $rds.Logon -Labels $rds.LogonDays -NoHistory `
            -ValueSuffix ' s' -ShowGrid -GridLineCount 3 -Minimum 0 `
            -WarningThreshold 30 -CriticalThreshold 60
    }

    # Bottom band: seats used against the limit, CPU and memory. Sessions
    # turn amber at 80 % of the limit and red at 95 %.
    if ($rds.Available) {
        $card = @{ Region = 'Bottom'; Height = [int](180 * $scale) }
        $split = "$($rds.Active) active, $($rds.Disconnected) disconnected"
        New-BGInfoMetric @card -Label 'Sessions' -Value $sessions `
            -Unit "of $($rds.SessionLimit)" -Caption $split `
            -History $rds.SessionHistory -HistoryMaximum $rds.SessionLimit `
            -WarningThreshold ($rds.SessionLimit * 0.8) `
            -CriticalThreshold ($rds.SessionLimit * 0.95)
        New-BGInfoMetric @card -Label 'CPU' -Value $rds.Cpu[-1] -Unit '%' `
            -Caption 'last 3 hours' -History $rds.Cpu -HistoryMaximum 100 `
            -WarningThreshold 70 -CriticalThreshold 85
        New-BGInfoMetric @card -Label 'Memory' -Value $memory -Unit '%' `
            -Caption "$($rds.MemoryGB) of $($rds.TotalGB) GB in use" `
            -History $rds.MemoryHistory -HistoryMaximum 100 `
            -WarningThreshold 80 -CriticalThreshold 90
        if ($rds.ProfileSizeTB) {
            $used = [Math]::Round(100 * $rds.ProfileUsedTB / $rds.ProfileSizeTB)
            $usage = "$($rds.ProfileUsedTB) of $($rds.ProfileSizeTB) TB on " +
                $rds.ProfileShare
            New-BGInfoMetric @card -Label 'Profile share' -Unit '%' `
                -Value $used -Caption $usage `
                -WarningThreshold 75 -CriticalThreshold 90
        }
    }
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory `
    -OutputFileName "rds-session-host-$($Theme.ToLower()).png"
#endregion

        )

        SessionHistory = @(2, 5, 9, 12, 14, 16, 17, 18, 18, 19, 19, 19)
        MemoryHistory  = @(31, 38, 45, 50, 54, 57, 58, 60, 61, 61, 62, 62)

        Containers   = [ordered] @{

            'olaf.b'  = 19.8

    }

#region Presentation: reads only $rds

} else { 0 }

    # A wide right column so the session table keeps every column readable.

    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Restart' -Value $rds.Restart

    # container is close to its cap (amber from 80 %, red from 90 %).
    if (@($rds.Sessions).Count -gt 0) {
        $rds.Sessions | Sort-Object Cpu -Descending |
            Select-Object User, State, Idle,
                @{ Name = 'CPU'; Expression = { "$($_.Cpu) %" } },
                @{ Name = 'Memory'; Expression = { "$($_.MemoryGB) GB" } } |
            New-BGInfoTable -Region Right -Title 'Who is on it' `
                -Note "$(@($rds.Sessions).Count) of $sessions by CPU" `
                -StatusColumn State -StatusMap @{ Active = 'Ok'; Disconnected = 'Warning' }
    }
    if ($rds.Containers.Count -gt 0) {
        $percent = foreach ($size in $rds.Containers.Values) {
            [Math]::Round(100 * $size / $rds.ProfileCapGB)
        }
        $title = 'Largest FSLogix containers  ·  ' +
            "cap $($rds.ProfileCapGB) GB"
        New-BGInfoChart -Region Right -Id 'containers' -Title $title `
            -Kind ProgressBar -Values $percent -Labels @($rds.Containers.Keys) `
            -Maximum 100 -ValueSuffix ' %' -NoHistory -NoProgressHandles `
            -ShowLatestValue:$false -ShowDataLabels `
            -WarningThreshold 80 -CriticalThreshold 90
    }

    # Center, under the text: how long sign-ins took over two weeks. A spike
    # usually means a GPO, profile or antivirus change.
    if (@($rds.Logon).Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoChart -Region Center -Id 'logon' `
            -Title 'Average logon  ·  last 14 days' `
            -Kind Bar -Values $rds.Logon -Labels $rds.LogonDays -NoHistory `
            -ValueSuffix ' s' -ShowGrid -GridLineCount 3 -Minimum 0 `
            -WarningThreshold 30 -CriticalThreshold 60
    }

    # Bottom band: seats used against the limit, CPU and memory. Sessions
    # turn amber at 80 % of the limit and red at 95 %.
    if ($rds.Available) {
        $card = @{ Region = 'Bottom'; Height = [int](180 * $scale) }
        $split = "$($rds.Active) active, $($rds.Disconnected) disconnected"
        New-BGInfoMetric @card -Label 'Sessions' -Value $sessions `
            -Unit "of $($rds.SessionLimit)" -Caption $split `
            -History $rds.SessionHistory -HistoryMaximum $rds.SessionLimit `
            -WarningThreshold ($rds.SessionLimit * 0.8) `
            -CriticalThreshold ($rds.SessionLimit * 0.95)
        New-BGInfoMetric @card -Label 'CPU' -Value $rds.Cpu[-1] -Unit '%' `
            -Caption 'last 3 hours' -History $rds.Cpu -HistoryMaximum 100 `
            -WarningThreshold 70 -CriticalThreshold 85
        New-BGInfoMetric @card -Label 'Memory' -Value $memory -Unit '%' `
            -Caption "$($rds.MemoryGB) of $($rds.TotalGB) GB in use" `
            -History $rds.MemoryHistory -HistoryMaximum 100 `
            -WarningThreshold 80 -CriticalThreshold 90
        if ($rds.ProfileSizeTB) {
            $used = [Math]::Round(100 * $rds.ProfileUsedTB / $rds.ProfileSizeTB)
            $usage = "$($rds.ProfileUsedTB) of $($rds.ProfileSizeTB) TB on " +
                $rds.ProfileShare
            New-BGInfoMetric @card -Label 'Profile share' -Unit '%' `
                -Value $used -Caption $usage `
                -WarningThreshold 75 -CriticalThreshold 90
        }
    }
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory `
    -OutputFileName "rds-session-host-$($Theme.ToLower()).png"
#endregion
features: Session table in a wide right column
Logon-time bars with the spike in amber
FSLogix container bars against the cap
Four metric cards with sparklines

        Group     = 'AG-FINANCE'
        Role      = 'Primary'
        Listener  = 'sqlfin.corp.contoso.com'
        # msdb.dbo.sysjobs and sysjobschedules for your backup jobs, or the
        # schedule in your backup product
        BackupJob = 'Full nightly 02:00, log every 15 min'

        #   SELECT DISTINCT vs.volume_mount_point, vs.total_bytes,
        #       vs.available_bytes

        #   CROSS APPLY sys.dm_os_volume_stats(f.database_id, f.file_id) vs
        # and Get-Volume or Get-PSDrive for the backup target.
        Drives    = [ordered] @{

        }

        Databases = @(

                LogMinutes = 11; Recovery = 'Full'; State = 'Online' }
        )
        # SQLServer:SQL Statistics\Batch Requests/sec from
        # sys.dm_os_performance_counters, sampled every 10 minutes
        Batches   = @(820, 940, 1180, 1460, 1720, 1650, 1540, 1810, 2050, 1930,
            1760, 1880)
    }
}

$fallback = [pscustomobject] @{
    Available = $false; Name = $env:COMPUTERNAME; Instance = 'unknown'

<#

    server: are the databases on it safe? That means a recent full backup,
    log backups that keep up, and replicas that hold a current copy. The
    status line names the worst database; the bottom table shows every one.

    The data block returns plain values; the presentation block only reads
    them. Comments name the command or source that supplies each value.
    dbatools (Get-DbaDatabase, Get-DbaAgReplica) returns the same facts if
    you prefer it to plain T-SQL through Invoke-Sqlcmd.
#>
param(
    [ValidateSet('Light', 'Dark')]
    [string] $Theme = 'Dark',
    [int] $Width = 1920,
    [int] $Height = 1080,
    [string] $OutputDirectory = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'Output')
)

Import-Module (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\PowerBGInfo.psd1') -Force

function Get-SqlServerSafety {

        # replica) and the listener from sys.availability_group_listeners
        Group     = 'AG-FINANCE'
        Role      = 'Primary'
        Listener  = 'sqlfin.corp.contoso.com'
        # msdb.dbo.sysjobs and sysjobschedules for your backup jobs, or the
        # schedule in your backup product
        BackupJob = 'Full nightly 02:00, log every 15 min'
        # Percent used per volume that holds database files:

        #   FROM sys.master_files f
        #   CROSS APPLY sys.dm_os_volume_stats(f.database_id, f.file_id) vs
        # and Get-Volume or Get-PSDrive for the backup target.
        Drives    = [ordered] @{

        }

        # secondary_lag_seconds column
        Replicas  = @(
            @{ Text = 'SQL-FIN-01  ·  primary'; Value = 'this server'
                Status = 'Ok' }
            @{ Text = 'SQL-FIN-02  ·  synchronous'; Value = 'synchronized'
                Status = 'Ok' }

        #   SELECT database_name, type, MAX(backup_finish_date)
        #   FROM msdb.dbo.backupset GROUP BY database_name, type
        # type D is a full backup, L a log backup.
        Databases = @(
            [pscustomobject] @{ Name = 'Finance'; SizeGB = 412; FullHours = 6
                LogMinutes = 12; Recovery = 'Full'; State = 'Online' }

                LogMinutes = 15; Recovery = 'Full'; State = 'Online' }

#endregion

#region Presentation: reads only $sql
$scale = [Math]::Round($Height / 1080, 2)
$look = New-BGInfoTheme Corporate -Mode $Theme -Scale $scale

# One rule for every database: a full backup within 26 hours and a log
# backup within 30 minutes is OK; a week without a full backup is critical.
function Format-Age([double] $Hours) {
    if ($Hours -ge 48) { "$([Math]::Round($Hours / 24)) days" }
    elseif ($Hours -ge 1) { "$([Math]::Round($Hours)) h" }
    else { "$([Math]::Round($Hours * 60)) min" }
}
$rows = foreach ($db in $sql.Databases) {
    $status = if ($db.State -ne 'Online' -or $db.FullHours -gt 168) {
        'Critical'
    }
    elseif ($db.FullHours -gt 26 -or $db.LogMinutes -gt 30) { 'Warning' }
    else { 'OK' }
    $log = if ($null -eq $db.LogMinutes) {
        "$($db.Recovery.ToLower()) recovery"
    } else { Format-Age ($db.LogMinutes / 60) }
    [pscustomobject] @{
        Database    = $db.Name
        Size        = "$($db.SizeGB) GB"
        'Last full' = Format-Age $db.FullHours
        'Last log'  = $log
        Status      = $status
        Order       = @{ Critical = 0; Warning = 1; OK = 2 }[$status]
        Hours       = $db.FullHours
    }
}
$rows = @($rows | Sort-Object Order, Database)
$worst = $rows | Select-Object -First 1

New-BGInfo -Theme $look -Target File {
    New-BGInfoBackground -Width $Width -Height $Height -Pattern Grid `
        -PatternSpacing ([int](48 * $scale))
    New-BGInfoLayout -ColumnWidth ([int](540 * $scale))

    $edition = $sql.Edition.Split(',')[0].ToUpper()
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name "$($sql.Version.ToUpper())  ·  $edition" -Accent `
        -FontSize ([int](15 * $scale)) -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $sql.Name -FontSize ([int](72 * $scale)) `
        -FontWeight 600
    if ($sql.Group) {
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name "$($sql.Role) replica of $($sql.Group)" -Accent `
            -FontSize ([int](26 * $scale)) -FontWeight 600
    }
    if (-not $worst) {
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name '●  Database data unavailable' -Status Info `
            -FontWeight 600
    } elseif ($worst.Status -eq 'OK') {
        $text = "All $($rows.Count) databases backed up on schedule"
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name "●  $text" -Status Ok -FontWeight 600
    } else {
        $issues = @($rows | Where-Object Status -NE 'OK').Count
        $text = "$($worst.Database): last full backup $($worst.'Last full') ago"
        if ($issues -gt 1) { $text += "  ·  $($issues - 1) more to check" }
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name "●  $text" -Status $worst.Status -FontWeight 600
    }
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Instance' -Value $sql.Instance
    $tier = $sql.Edition.Split(',')[-1].Trim()
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Build' -Value "$($sql.Build), $tier"
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Listener' -Value $sql.Listener
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Backups' -Value $sql.BackupJob

    # Right column: where the data is, colored by the age of its last full
    # backup, then the replicas that hold a copy of it.
    if ($rows.Count -gt 0) {
        $sql.Databases | New-BGInfoTreemap -Region Right `
            -Title 'Data by database' `
            -Note 'color: last full backup' -ValueProperty SizeGB `
            -ValueSuffix ' GB' -ColorProperty FullHours `
            -WarningThreshold 26 -CriticalThreshold 168 `
            -Height ([int](360 * $scale))
    }
    if (@($sql.Replicas).Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoList -Region Right -Title $sql.Group -Note 'replicas' `
            -Item $sql.Replicas
    }

    # Center, under the text: the workload right now.
    if (@($sql.Batches).Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoChart -Region Center -Id 'batches' `
            -Title 'Batch requests / s  ·  last 2 hours' -Kind Area `
            -Values $sql.Batches -NoHistory -ShowGrid -GridLineCount 2
    }

    # Bottom band: every database, problems first, and the room left for
    # data, logs and backups (amber from 80 %, red from 90 %).
    $band = @{ Region = 'Bottom'; Height = [int](400 * $scale) }
    if ($rows.Count -gt 0) {
        $rows | New-BGInfoTable @band -Title 'Databases' `
            -Note 'from msdb backup history' -Width ([int](1240 * $scale)) `
            -Property Database, Size, 'Last full', 'Last log', Status `
            -StatusColumn Status
    }
    if ($sql.Drives.Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoChart @band -Id 'drives' `
            -Title 'Space for data, logs and backups' `
            -Kind ProgressBar -Values @($sql.Drives.Values) `
            -Labels @($sql.Drives.Keys) -Maximum 100 -ValueSuffix ' %' `
            -NoHistory -NoProgressHandles -ShowLatestValue:$false `
            -ShowDataLabels `
            -WarningThreshold 80 -CriticalThreshold 90
    }
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory `
    -OutputFileName "sql-server-$($Theme.ToLower()).png"
#endregion

Workload area chart

    $share | Select-Object *, @{
        Name = 'Percent'
        Expression = { [Math]::Round(100 * $share.UsedGB / $share.QuotaGB) }
    }
}
$shares = @($shares | Sort-Object Percent -Descending)
$fullest = $shares | Select-Object -First 1

New-BGInfo -Theme $look -Target File {
    New-BGInfoBackground -Width $Width -Height $Height -GradientAngle 160
    New-BGInfoLayout -ColumnWidth ([int](500 * $scale))

    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Shadow copies' -Value $fs.Shadow
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'System' -Value $fs.Os

            -Note 'color: quota used' -ValueProperty UsedGB `
            -GroupProperty Group -ValueSuffix ' GB' -ColorProperty Percent `
            -WarningThreshold 80 -CriticalThreshold 90

            -Value $fs.OpenFiles[-1] `

            -History $fs.OpenFiles -Height ([int](150 * $scale))

        } else { 'not growing' }

        elseif ($weeks -ge 4) { 'Warning' } else { 'Critical' }

        }

            -Value $weekly -Unit 'GB / week' -Caption $caption -Status $runway `
            -History $deltas -HistoryKind Bars -Height ([int](150 * $scale))
    }

    # Bottom band: quota alerts this week and the DFS Replication backlog.
    $band = @{ Region = 'Bottom'; Height = [int](280 * $scale) }
    if (@($fs.Alerts).Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoList @band -Title 'Quota alerts' -Note 'FSRM, last 7 days' `
            -Item $fs.Alerts -Width ([int](620 * $scale))
    }

        $fs.Backlog | Sort-Object { $_.State -eq 'OK' }, Folder |
            Select-Object Folder, Partner,
                @{ Name = 'Backlog'
                    Expression = { '{0:N0} files' -f $_.Files } },
                @{ Name = 'Last sync'; Expression = { $_.Last } }, State |
            New-BGInfoTable @band -Title 'DFS Replication' `
                -Note 'outbound backlog' -StatusColumn State
    }
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory `
    -OutputFileName "file-server-$($Theme.ToLower()).png"
#endregion

<#
    Certificate authority. The question for the PKI administrator at this
    console: will anything expire soon on this CA? Certificates first, then
    the CA's own certificate, the revocation lists it publishes and whether
    clients can reach them.

    The data block returns plain values; the presentation block only reads
    them. Comments name the command or source that supplies each value.
#>
param(
    [ValidateSet('Light', 'Dark')]
    [string] $Theme = 'Dark',
    [int] $Width = 1920,
    [int] $Height = 1080,
    [string] $OutputDirectory = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'Output')
)

#region Data: your logic goes here
function Get-CertificateAuthorityHealth {
    $today = Get-Date '2026-10-16 07:00'
    [pscustomobject] @{
        Available = $true
        Now       = $today
        # certutil -cainfo name, certutil -cainfo type, or PSPKI:
        #   Get-CertificationAuthority -ComputerName $env:COMPUTERNAME
        Name      = 'Contoso Issuing CA 02'
        Type      = 'Enterprise subordinate CA'
        Host      = 'PKI-ISS-02.corp.contoso.com'
        Parent    = 'Contoso Root CA (offline)'
        # certutil -getreg CA\CSP\CNGHashAlgorithm and the CA certificate
        Key       = 'RSA 4096 · SHA-256'
        # (Get-CertificationAuthority).Certificate.NotAfter
        CaExpires = Get-Date '2031-03-14'
        # Issued certificates by expiry day for the next 90 days:
        #   certutil -view -restrict ("Disposition=20,NotAfter>=$today," +
        #       "NotAfter<=$($today.AddDays(90))") `
        #       -out "RequestID,CommonName,NotAfter,CertificateTemplate" csv
        # or PSPKI:
        #   Get-IssuedRequest -Filter "NotAfter -le $($today.AddDays(90))"
        Expiring  = foreach ($day in 1..90) {
            $date = $today.Date.AddDays($day)
            $weekend = $date.DayOfWeek -in 'Saturday', 'Sunday'
            $value = if ($weekend) { 0 } else { ($day * 7) % 3 }
            # A batch of web server certificates issued together last year.
            if ($day -eq 12) { $value = 9 }
            if ($day -eq 41) { $value = 6 }
            if ($day -eq 67) { $value = 5 }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Date = $date; Value = $value }
        }
        # Get-CATemplate, with issued and expiring counts per template from
        # Get-IssuedRequest -Property CertificateTemplate | Group-Object, and
        # the renewal mode from the template's enrollment flags
        Templates = @(
            [pscustomobject] @{ Template = 'Web Server'
                Issued = 412; 'Expire in 90 d' = 34
                Renewal = 'Manual'; State = 'Attention' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Template = 'Computer'
                Issued = 1880; 'Expire in 90 d' = 22
                Renewal = 'Autoenrollment'; State = 'OK' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Template = 'User'
                Issued = 2340; 'Expire in 90 d' = 19
                Renewal = 'Autoenrollment'; State = 'OK' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Template = 'Kerberos Authentication'
                Issued = 12; 'Expire in 90 d' = 3
                Renewal = 'Autoenrollment'; State = 'OK' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Template = 'Code Signing'
                Issued = 8; 'Expire in 90 d' = 2
                Renewal = 'Manual'; State = 'Attention' }
        )
        # The CRLs this CA publishes: certutil -dump <file>.crl ("Next Update"),
        # or PSPKI Get-CRLValidityPeriod. Reachability of every AIA and CDP
        # URL as pkiview.msc checks it: PSPKI Get-EnterprisePKIHealthStatus,
        # or certutil -verify -urlfetch <certificate>.
        Crl       = Get-Date '2026-10-18 06:00'
        DeltaCrl  = Get-Date '2026-10-16 18:00'
        Checks    = @(
            @{ Text = 'AIA · http'; Value = 'reachable'; Status = 'Ok' }
            @{ Text = 'CDP · http'; Value = 'reachable'; Status = 'Ok' }
            @{ Text = 'CDP · ldap'; Value = '1 of 2 DCs'; Status = 'Warning' }
            @{ Text = 'OCSP responder'; Value = 'signing cert ok'
                Status = 'Ok' }
        )
        # Failed requests per day for 30 days: PSPKI Get-FailedRequest, or
        # certutil -view -restrict "Disposition=30" grouped by SubmittedWhen
        Failed    = @(1, 0, 2, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 3, 1, 0, 2, 0, 0, 1, 2, 1, 0, 1,
            0, 0, 2, 1, 3, 2, 0, 0, 2, 7, 4)
    }
}

$fallback = [pscustomobject] @{
    Available = $false; Now = Get-Date; Name = $env:COMPUTERNAME
    Type = 'unknown'; Host = 'unknown'; Parent = 'unknown'; Key = 'unknown'
    CaExpires = $null
    Expiring = @(); Templates = @(); Crl = $null; DeltaCrl = $null
    Checks = @(); Failed = @()

$source = @{
