        -Accent -FontSize ([int](15 * $scale)) -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $ca.Name -FontSize ([int](64 * $scale)) `
        -FontWeight 600
    if (-not $ca.Available) {
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name '●  CA data unavailable' -Status Info `
            -FontWeight 600
    } elseif ($soon -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name "●  $soon certificates expire within 30 days" `
            -Status Warning -FontWeight 600
    } else {
        $text = 'Nothing expires within 30 days; CRL publishes ' +
            (Format-Until $ca.Crl)
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name "●  $text" -Status Ok -FontWeight 600
    }
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Host' -Value $ca.Host
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Parent' -Value $ca.Parent
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Key' -Value $ca.Key
    if ($null -ne $ca.Crl) {
        $crl = "next update $(Format-Until $ca.Crl), " +
            $ca.Crl.ToString('ddd d MMM HH:mm')
        New-BGInfoValue -Name 'CRL' -Value $crl
        $delta = "next update $(Format-Until $ca.DeltaCrl), " +
            $ca.DeltaCrl.ToString('HH:mm')
        New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Delta CRL' -Value $delta
    }

    if ($ca.Available) {
        # Right column: the CA's own certificate, then what clients reach.
        $caDays = [int] ($ca.CaExpires - $ca.Now).TotalDays
        New-BGInfoMetric -Region Right -Label 'CA certificate' -Value $caDays `
            -Unit 'days left' `
            -Caption "valid until $($ca.CaExpires.ToString('d MMM yyyy'))" `
            -WarningThreshold 730 -CriticalThreshold 365 `
            -ThresholdDirection Below -Height ([int](150 * $scale))
        # Bars draw bottom up, so the nearest window goes last to sit on top.
        New-BGInfoChart -Region Right -Id 'expiry' `
            -Title 'Expiring certificates' -Kind HorizontalBar `
            -Values ($within90 - $within60), ($within60 - $soon), $soon `
            -Labels '61–90 days', '31–60 days', '0–30 days' `
            -Palette @($look.Muted, $look.Accent, $look.Warning) `
            -ShowDataLabels -ShowLatestValue:$false -NoHistory `
            -Height ([int](230 * $scale))
        New-BGInfoList -Region Right -Title 'AIA and CDP' -Note 'pkiview' `
            -Item $ca.Checks

        # Center: what this CA issues, and how much of it renews itself.
        $ca.Templates | New-BGInfoTable -Region Center -Title 'Templates' `
            -Note 'manual renewal needs a person' -StatusColumn State

        # Bottom band: every expiry day in the next 90 days, and failures.
        $band = @{ Region = 'Bottom'; Height = [int](280 * $scale) }
        $ca.Expiring | New-BGInfoCalendarHeatmap @band `
            -Title 'Expiry calendar' -Note 'next 90 days' `
            -Color $look.Warning -Width ([int](480 * $scale))
        New-BGInfoChart @band -Id 'failed' `
            -Title 'Failed requests  ·  last 30 days' `
            -Kind Bar -Values $ca.Failed -ShowLatestValue `
            -ValueSuffix ' today' -WarningThreshold 5 -CriticalThreshold 20 `
            -NoHistory
    }
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory `
    -OutputFileName "certificate-authority-$($Theme.ToLower()).png"
#endregion
features: Calendar of expiry dates over the next 90 days
30, 60 and 90-day expiry bars
Failed requests per day, coloured by threshold
Template table with renewal state

scenarios.title: Backup server
scenarios.purpose: Whether last night's backups worked, and which jobs need a retry before tonight.
scenarios.source:
<#
    Backup server. The question for the administrator who signs in first
    thing in the morning: did last night's backups work, and if not, which
    jobs need attention before tonight's window?

    The data block returns plain values; the presentation block only reads
    them. Comments name the command or source that supplies each value.
    The samples are product-neutral: swap in your backup product's API,
    for example Get-VBRJob and Get-VBRBackupSession (Veeam), or
    Get-WBSummary and Get-WBJob (Windows Server Backup).
#>
param(
    [ValidateSet('Light', 'Dark')]
    [string] $Theme = 'Dark',
    [int] $Width = 1920,
    [int] $Height = 1080,
    [string] $OutputDirectory = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'Output')
)

Import-Module (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\PowerBGInfo.psd1') -Force

#region Data: your logic goes here
function Get-BackupStatus {
    $today = Get-Date '2026-10-16 07:50'
    [pscustomobject] @{
        Available = $true
        # $env:COMPUTERNAME and (Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem).Domain
        Name      = 'BKP-AMS-01'
        Domain    = 'corp.contoso.com'
        # Results of the sessions that ran last night, for example
        #   Get-VBRBackupSession | Where-Object CreationTime -GT $since |
        #       Group-Object { $_.Result }
        # or (Get-WBJob -Previous 1).JobState for Windows Server Backup.
        Succeeded = 47
        Warning   = 1
        Failed    = 1
        # First session start and last session end of the night
        Started   = '22:00'
        Finished  = '04:12'
        Protected = '18.4 TB from 212 machines'
        # (Get-WBSummary).NextBackupTime, or the job schedule:
        # Get-VBRJob | Get-VBRJobScheduleOptions
        NextWindow = '22:00'
        NextDetail = 'tonight · 49 jobs · in 14 h'
        # Your retention policy, or Get-VBRJob | Get-VBRJobOptions
        Retention  = '30 daily, 12 monthly'
        # Failed and warning sessions with their reason, for example
        # (Get-VBRBackupSession -Name <job>).Logger.GetLog().UpdatedRecords
        Attention = @(
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Job = 'SQL-PRD cluster'; Target = 'SQL-PRD-02'
                Reason = 'VSS writer timed out'
                Retries = '3 of 3'; State = 'Failed'
            }
            [pscustomobject] @{
                Job = 'File servers'; Target = 'FS-AMS-03'
                Reason = 'Skipped 12 locked files'
                Retries = '1 of 3'; State = 'Warning'
            }
        )
        # Get-VBRBackupRepository, then free space per repository; for a
        # local repository Get-Volume -DriveLetter R gives Size and
        # SizeRemaining. Percent used.
        Repositories = [ordered] @{
            'Primary · R:'   = 71
            'Archive · S:'   = 86
            'Object storage' = 54
        }
        # Copies off this server. The immutable lock comes from your
        # repository settings, or from the bucket itself:
        #   Get-S3ObjectLockConfiguration -BucketName <bucket> (AWS.Tools.S3)
        # The offsite copy lag from your backup copy job, for example
        #   Get-VBRBackupCopyJob and its last session.
        Copies = @(
            @{ Text = 'Immutable copy'; Value = 'locked 30 days'
                Status = 'Ok' }
            @{ Text = 'Offsite copy'; Value = 'synced 05:40'; Status = 'Ok' }
            @{ Text = 'Tape export'; Value = 'Sat 06:00'; Status = 'Info' }
            @{ Text = 'Restore test'; Value = '9 days ago'; Status = 'Warning' }
        )
        # Percent of jobs that succeeded on each of the last 14 nights,
        # oldest first, from the same session history as below.
        Rate = @(100, 100, 100, 100, 71, 90, 100,
            100, 100, 94, 100, 100, 100, 96)
        # Nights with failed or warning jobs, from the session history:
        #   Get-VBRBackupSession | Where-Object Result -NE 'Success' |
        #       Group-Object { $_.CreationTime.Date }
        # A night without a problem is simply not in the list.
        History = foreach ($day in 1..364) {
            $value = if ($day % 9 -eq 0) { 1 }
            elseif ($day % 23 -eq 5) { 3 } else { 0 }
            # A storage outage ten days ago failed 14 jobs.
            if ($day -eq 10) { $value = 14 }
            if ($day -eq 9) { $value = 5 }
            if ($day -eq 1) { $value = 2 }
            if ($value -gt 0) {
                [pscustomobject] @{
                    Date = $today.Date.AddDays(-$day); Value = $value
                }
            }
        }
        Now = $today
    }
}

$fallback = [pscustomobject] @{
    Available = $false; Name = $env:COMPUTERNAME; Domain = 'unknown'
    Succeeded = 0; Warning = 0; Failed = 0; Started = ''; Finished = ''
    Protected = 'unknown'; NextWindow = 'unknown'; NextDetail = ''
    Retention = 'unknown'; Attention = @()
    Repositories = [ordered] @{}; Copies = @(); Rate = @()
    History = @()
    Now = Get-Date
}
$source = @{
    Name           = 'Backup status'
    TimeoutSeconds = 30
    ScriptBlock    = ${function:Get-BackupStatus}
    Default        = $fallback
}
$backup = Invoke-BGInfoDataSource @source
#endregion

#region Presentation: reads only $backup
$scale = [Math]::Round($Height / 1080, 2)
$look = New-BGInfoTheme Graphite -Mode $Theme -Scale $scale -Accent '#2DD4BF'
$total = $backup.Succeeded + $backup.Warning + $backup.Failed
$glow = if ($Theme -eq 'Dark') { '#2DD4BF26' } else { '#5EEAD455' }

New-BGInfo -Theme $look -Target File {
    New-BGInfoLayout -ColumnWidth ([int](470 * $scale))
    New-BGInfoBackground -Width $Width -Height $Height -Glow @(
        New-BGInfoBackgroundGlow -X 0.0 -Y 0.0 -Radius 0.55 -Color $glow
    )

    $heading = "BACKUP SERVER  ·  $($backup.Name)  ·  " +
        $backup.Domain.ToUpper()
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $heading `
        -Accent -FontSize ([int](15 * $scale)) -FontWeight 700
    if ($total -eq 0) {
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'No results' -FontSize ([int](96 * $scale)) `
            -FontWeight 700
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name '●  Backup results unavailable' -Status Info `
            -FontWeight 600
    } else {
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name "$($backup.Succeeded) of $total" `
            -FontSize ([int](112 * $scale)) -FontWeight 700
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'jobs succeeded last night' `
            -FontSize ([int](26 * $scale)) -FontWeight 600
        $problems = @()
        if ($backup.Failed -gt 0) { $problems += "$($backup.Failed) failed" }
        if ($backup.Warning -gt 0) {
            $problems += "$($backup.Warning) with warnings"
        }
        if ($backup.Failed -gt 0) {
            $text = "$($problems -join ', '): retry before tonight"
            New-BGInfoLabel -Name "●  $text" -Status Critical -FontWeight 600
        } elseif ($backup.Warning -gt 0) {
            New-BGInfoLabel -Name "●  $($problems -join ', ')" `
                -Status Warning -FontWeight 600
        } else {
            New-BGInfoLabel -Name '●  Every job succeeded' -Status Ok `
                -FontWeight 600
        }
    }
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Last night' `
        -Value "$($backup.Started) – $($backup.Finished)"
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Protected' -Value $backup.Protected
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Retention' -Value $backup.Retention

    # Right column: when the next run starts, where the copies of the data
    # are, and how full each repository is (amber at 80 %, red at 90 %).
    New-BGInfoMetric -Region Right -Label 'Next window' `
        -Value $backup.NextWindow `
        -Caption $backup.NextDetail -Status Info -Height ([int](170 * $scale))
    if (@($backup.Copies).Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoList -Region Right -Title 'Copies' -Note '3-2-1 rule' `
            -Item $backup.Copies
    }
    if ($backup.Repositories.Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoChart -Region Right -Id 'repositories' `
            -Title 'Repository space used' `
            -Kind ProgressBar -Values @($backup.Repositories.Values) `
            -Labels @($backup.Repositories.Keys) -Maximum 100 `
            -ValueSuffix ' %' -NoProgressHandles -ShowLatestValue:$false `
            -NoHistory -ShowDataLabels -WarningThreshold 80 `
            -CriticalThreshold 90 -Height ([int](220 * $scale))
    }

    # Center: only the jobs that need someone, failures first.
    if (@($backup.Attention).Count -gt 0) {
        $backup.Attention | Sort-Object { $_.State -ne 'Failed' } |
            New-BGInfoTable -Region Center -Title 'Needs attention' `
                -Note 'last night' -StatusColumn State
    }

    # Bottom band: a year of nights, so a bad night stands out, and the
    # success rate of the last two weeks (amber below 98 %, red below 90 %).
    $band = @{ Region = 'Bottom'; Height = [int](270 * $scale) }
    if (@($backup.History).Count -gt 0) {
        @($backup.History) | New-BGInfoCalendarHeatmap @band `
            -Title 'Nights with failed or warning jobs' -Note 'last 12 months' `
            -Color $look.Critical -Width ([int](1240 * $scale))
    }
    if (@($backup.Rate).Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoChart @band -Id 'rate' `
            -Title 'Succeeded · last 14 nights' -Kind Bar `
            -Values $backup.Rate -Minimum 0 -Maximum 100 -ValueSuffix ' %' `
            -ShowGrid -GridLineCount 3 -ShowLatestValue:$false -NoHistory `
            -WarningThreshold 98 -CriticalThreshold 90 -ThresholdDirection Below
    }
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory `
    -OutputFileName "backup-server-$($Theme.ToLower()).png"
#endregion
features: A year of nights as a calendar heatmap
Success-rate bars coloured by threshold
Repository progress bars at 80 and 90 %
Status list for the copies

scenarios.title: Jump host
scenarios.purpose: The rules of a privileged access host: who is elevated, what is recorded and what is never allowed.
scenarios.source:
<#
    Jump host. The question for the administrator who just connected: what
    are the rules on this machine? It says who is signed in and how they
    were elevated, that the session is recorded, which tools belong here,
    what never to do here, and who else is connected right now.

    The data block returns plain values; the presentation block only reads
    them. Comments name the command or source that supplies each value.
#>
param(
    [ValidateSet('Light', 'Dark')]
    [string] $Theme = 'Dark',
    [int] $Width = 1920,
    [int] $Height = 1080,
    [string] $OutputDirectory = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'Output')
)

Import-Module (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\PowerBGInfo.psd1') -Force

#region Data: your logic goes here
function Get-JumpHostRules {
    [pscustomobject] @{
        Available = $true
        # $env:COMPUTERNAME and $env:USERDNSDOMAIN
        Name      = 'JMP-T0-01'
        Domain    = 'corp.contoso.com'
        Tier      = 'Tier 0'
        # whoami, or [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent().Name
        User      = 'CONTOSO\adm-t0.avery'
        # whoami /groups lists the admin group and the
        # "Mandatory Label\High Mandatory Level" of an elevated token. The end
        # time comes from your PIM or PAM tool, for example
        # Get-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleAssignmentScheduleInstance.
        Elevation = 'Domain Admins until 11:40'
        # Get-MgAuditLogSignIn -Filter "userPrincipalName eq '...'" -Top 1,
        # its authenticationDetails
        Mfa       = 'FIDO2 key at 09:38'
        # Your session recording product, or the policy text it enforces
        Recording = 'Recorded and reviewed, kept 90 days'
        # Your access policy, published where the admins can scan it
        Policy    = 'https://intranet.contoso.com/policy/admin-access'
        # The tools installed for this tier, from your build definition, or
        # Get-Package / Get-WindowsCapability -Online |
        #     Where-Object State -EQ Installed
        Allowed   = @(
            @{ Text = 'Active Directory tools'; Value = 'RSAT'; Status = 'Ok' }
            @{ Text = 'PowerShell 7'; Value = 'signed scripts'; Status = 'Ok' }
            @{ Text = 'Group Policy Management'; Value = 'GPMC'; Status = 'Ok' }
            @{ Text = 'Remote Desktop'; Value = 'tier 0 only'; Status = 'Ok' }
        )
        # Your admin policy, in the words people remember
        Never     = @(
            @{ Text = 'No web browsing'; Value = 'proxy blocks it'
                Status = 'Critical' }
            @{ Text = 'No email or chat'; Value = 'not installed'
                Status = 'Critical' }
            @{ Text = 'No file copy to the internet'; Value = 'DLP enforced'
                Status = 'Critical' }
            @{ Text = 'No personal or shared accounts'; Value = 'named admins'
                Status = 'Critical' }
        )
        # query session (qwinsta), or Get-RDUserSession on a session host
        Sessions  = @(
            [pscustomobject] @{
                User = 'adm-t0.avery (you)'; From = 'PAW-T0-03'
                Since = '09:38'; State = 'Online'
            }
            [pscustomobject] @{
                User = 'adm-t0.morgan'; From = 'PAW-T0-07'
                Since = '08:12'; State = 'Online'
            }
            [pscustomobject] @{
                User = 'adm-t0.quinn'; From = 'PAW-T0-01'
                Since = 'yesterday 17:05'; State = 'Disconnected'
            }
        )
        # Get-LocalGroupMember -Group Administrators | Measure-Object
        LocalAdmins = '2 groups, no users'
        # Your baseline scan time; each line below from its own check:
        BaselineAt = 'today 06:00'
        Baseline  = @(
            # Get-MpComputerStatus: RealTimeProtectionEnabled,
            # AntivirusSignatureAge
            @{ Text = 'Defender real-time'; Value = 'on, 2 h old'
                Status = 'Ok' }
            # (Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard
            #   -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard).SecurityServicesRunning
            @{ Text = 'Credential Guard'; Value = 'running'; Status = 'Ok' }
            # Get-MgDeviceManagementManagedDevice: ComplianceState
            @{ Text = 'Intune compliance'; Value = 'compliant'; Status = 'Ok' }
            # Get-HotFix | Sort-Object InstalledOn | Select-Object -Last 1
            @{ Text = 'Security updates'; Value = '1 pending'
                Status = 'Warning' }
        )
    }
}

$fallback = [pscustomobject] @{
    Available = $false; Name = $env:COMPUTERNAME; Domain = 'unknown'; Tier = ''
    User = 'unknown'; Elevation = 'unknown'; Mfa = 'unknown'
    Recording = 'Assume this session is recorded'; Policy = ''
    Allowed = @(); Never = @(); Sessions = @(); LocalAdmins = 'unknown'
    BaselineAt = ''; Baseline = @()
}
$source = @{
    Name           = 'Jump host rules'
    TimeoutSeconds = 15
    ScriptBlock    = ${function:Get-JumpHostRules}
    Default        = $fallback
}
$jump = Invoke-BGInfoDataSource @source
#endregion

#region Presentation: reads only $jump
$scale = [Math]::Round($Height / 1080, 2)
# Violet marks the privileged tier; a deeper shade keeps contrast in light.
$accent = if ($Theme -eq 'Dark') { '#A78BFA' } else { '#7C3AED' }
$look = New-BGInfoTheme Midnight -Mode $Theme -Scale $scale -Accent $accent
$glow = if ($Theme -eq 'Dark') { '#7C3AED33' } else { '#C4B5FD66' }

New-BGInfo -Theme $look -Target File {
    New-BGInfoLayout -ColumnWidth ([int](470 * $scale))
    New-BGInfoBackground -Width $Width -Height $Height -GradientAngle 160 `
        -Glow @(
            New-BGInfoBackgroundGlow -X 0.0 -Y 0.0 -Radius 0.5 -Color $glow
            New-BGInfoBackgroundGlow -X 1.0 -Y 0.55 -Radius 0.35 -Color $glow
        )

    $heading = @('JUMP HOST', $jump.Tier.ToUpper(), $jump.Name,
        $jump.Domain.ToUpper()) | Where-Object { $_ }
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name ($heading -join '  ·  ') -Accent `
        -FontSize ([int](15 * $scale)) -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'Privileged access only' `
        -FontSize ([int](80 * $scale)) -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name "●  $($jump.Recording)" -Status Critical `
        -FontWeight 600
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Signed in' -Value $jump.User
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Elevation' -Value $jump.Elevation
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'MFA' -Value $jump.Mfa
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Local admins' -Value $jump.LocalAdmins

    # The rules nobody gets to bend, as large as the policy deserves.
    if (@($jump.Never).Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name ' ' -FontSize ([int](14 * $scale))
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'NEVER ON THIS HOST' -Accent `
            -FontSize ([int](15 * $scale)) -FontWeight 700
        foreach ($rule in $jump.Never) {
            New-BGInfoLabel -Name "✕  $($rule.Text)" -Status Critical `
                -FontSize ([int](30 * $scale)) -FontWeight 600
        }
    }

    # Right column: the policy to read, then the tools that belong here.
    if ($jump.Policy) {
        $link = [uri] $jump.Policy
        New-BGInfoQRCode -Region Right -Text $jump.Policy `
            -Title 'Access policy' `
            -Caption "$($link.Host)$($link.AbsolutePath)" `
            -Height ([int](360 * $scale))
    }
    if (@($jump.Allowed).Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoList -Region Right -Title 'Allowed here' -Item $jump.Allowed
    }

    # Bottom band: who else is connected, and the last baseline check.
    $band = @{ Region = 'Bottom'; Height = [int](250 * $scale) }
    if (@($jump.Sessions).Count -gt 0) {
        $jump.Sessions | New-BGInfoTable @band -Title 'Admin sessions' `
            -Note "$(@($jump.Sessions).Count) on this host" -StatusColumn State -StatusMap @{ Disconnected = 'Warning' }
    }
    if (@($jump.Baseline).Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoList @band -Title 'Security baseline' -Note $jump.BaselineAt `
            -Item $jump.Baseline -Width ([int](560 * $scale))
    }
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory `
    -OutputFileName "jump-host-$($Theme.ToLower()).png"
#endregion
features: Large rule labels as a poster
QR code to the access policy
Allowed tools and baseline status lists
Admin sessions table

scenarios.title: Linux server
scenarios.purpose: What this Linux box is, rendered headless under PowerShell 7.
scenarios.source:
<#
    Linux server. The question for whoever opens the console or the
    rendered status image: what is this box? Its name, distribution and
    kernel, how long it has been up and how loaded it is, how full its
    mounts are, which systemd units failed, what it listens on, when it was
    last updated and who owns it.

    PowerBGInfo renders headless on Linux under PowerShell 7 (preview), so
    -Target File writes the image for a console splash, a KVM or BMC
    screen, or a status page. The data block returns plain values; the
    presentation block only reads them. Comments name the pwsh-friendly
    command or file that supplies each value.
#>
param(
    [ValidateSet('Light', 'Dark')]
    [string] $Theme = 'Dark',
    [int] $Width = 1920,
    [int] $Height = 1080,
    [string] $OutputDirectory = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'Output')
)

Import-Module (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\PowerBGInfo.psd1') -Force

#region Data: your logic goes here
function Get-LinuxServerInfo {
    [pscustomobject] @{
        Available = $true
        # [System.Net.Dns]::GetHostName() and hostname --domain
        Name      = 'web-lnx-04'
        Domain    = 'corp.contoso.com'
        # $os = Get-Content /etc/os-release | ConvertFrom-StringData
        # $os.PRETTY_NAME.Trim('"')
        Distro    = 'Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS'
        # uname -r and uname -m
        Kernel    = '6.8.0-45-generic · x86_64'
        # Get-Uptime (PowerShell 7 reads /proc/uptime)
        Uptime    = '41 days, 6 h'
        # ip -json -4 addr show eth0 | ConvertFrom-Json
        Address   = '10.20.4.14 · eth0'
        # A file your provisioning writes, for example /etc/contoso/owner
        Owner     = 'Web Platform team'
        # (Get-Content /proc/loadavg) -split ' ' gives the 1, 5 and 15
        # minute averages; [Environment]::ProcessorCount the cores.
        Load      = @(1.42, 1.18, 0.97)
        Cores     = 8
        # The 1-minute average sampled every 15 minutes into a small file,
        # or sar -q from sysstat for the last six hours
        LoadHistory = @(0.8, 0.9, 1.1, 0.9, 1.0, 1.4, 2.6, 3.1, 2.2, 1.6, 1.3,
            1.2, 1.1, 1.0, 0.9, 1.1, 1.3, 1.2, 1.5, 1.6, 1.4, 1.3, 1.5, 1.42)
        # df -P --output=target,pcent | Select-Object -Skip 1, or
        # Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem (Used and Free). Percent used.
        Mounts    = [ordered] @{
            '/'                   = 58
            '/var'                = 83
            '/var/lib/postgresql' = 71
            '/boot'               = 34
        }
        # systemctl list-units --type=service --state=failed --plain --no-legend
        # and systemctl is-active for the services that matter here
        UnitCount = 214
        Units     = @(
            @{ Text = 'backup-sync.service'; Value = 'failed 02:00'
                Status = 'Critical' }
            @{ Text = 'nginx.service'; Value = 'running'; Status = 'Ok' }
            @{ Text = 'postgresql@16-main'; Value = 'running'; Status = 'Ok' }
            @{ Text = 'ssh.service'; Value = 'running'; Status = 'Ok' }
            @{ Text = 'node_exporter.service'; Value = 'running'
                Status = 'Ok' }
            @{ Text = 'certbot.timer'; Value = 'next 03:12'; Status = 'Info' }
        )
        # ss -Htlnp: listening TCP sockets with the owning process
        Listening = @(
            [pscustomobject] @{ Port = 22; Service = 'sshd'
                Bound = '0.0.0.0'; Exposed = 'Internal' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Port = 443; Service = 'nginx'
                Bound = '0.0.0.0'; Exposed = 'Public' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Port = 80; Service = 'nginx'
                Bound = '0.0.0.0'; Exposed = 'Redirect' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Port = 5432; Service = 'postgres'
                Bound = '127.0.0.1'; Exposed = 'Local' }
            [pscustomobject] @{ Port = 9100; Service = 'node_exporter'
                Bound = '10.20.4.14'; Exposed = 'Internal' }
        )
        # Select-String '^Start-Date|^Upgrade' /var/log/apt/history.log,
        # dnf history list on Red Hat family systems, and
        # apt list --upgradable for what is still pending
        Updates   = @(
            @{ Text = 'Pending'; Value = '3 security'; Status = 'Warning' }
            @{ Text = 'Mon 13 Oct · apt upgrade'; Value = '14 packages'
                Status = 'Ok' }
            @{ Text = 'Thu 09 Oct · unattended'; Value = 'openssl'
                Status = 'Ok' }
            @{ Text = 'Thu 02 Oct · unattended'; Value = 'linux-image'
                Status = 'Ok' }
        )
    }
}

$fallback = [pscustomobject] @{
    Available = $false; Name = [System.Net.Dns]::GetHostName(); Domain = ''
    Distro = 'unknown'; Kernel = 'unknown'; Uptime = 'unknown'
    Address = 'unknown'; Owner = 'unknown'; Load = @(); Cores = 0
    LoadHistory = @(); Mounts = [ordered] @{}; UnitCount = 0; Units = @()
    Listening = @(); Updates = @()
}
$source = @{
    Name           = 'Linux server'
    TimeoutSeconds = 15
    ScriptBlock    = ${function:Get-LinuxServerInfo}
    Default        = $fallback
}
$linux = Invoke-BGInfoDataSource @source
#endregion

#region Presentation: reads only $linux
$scale = [Math]::Round($Height / 1080, 2)
$look = New-BGInfoTheme Aurora -Mode $Theme -Scale $scale
# The host name in a terminal face, as it appears at the shell prompt.
$mono = 'Cascadia Mono, DejaVu Sans Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace'
$failed = @($linux.Units | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq 'Critical' })
$dots = if ($Theme -eq 'Dark') { '#FFFFFF10' } else { '#0F172A12' }

New-BGInfo -Theme $look -Target File {
    New-BGInfoLayout -ColumnWidth ([int](470 * $scale))
    New-BGInfoBackground -Width $Width -Height $Height -Pattern Dots `
        -PatternColor $dots -PatternSpacing ([int](26 * $scale))

    $heading = @('LINUX SERVER', $linux.Distro.ToUpper(),
        $linux.Domain.ToUpper()) | Where-Object { $_ }
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name ($heading -join '  ·  ') -Accent `
        -FontSize ([int](15 * $scale)) -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $linux.Name -FontFamilyName $mono `
        -FontSize ([int](76 * $scale)) -FontWeight 700
    if (-not $linux.Available) {
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name '●  Server data unavailable' -Status Info `
            -FontWeight 600
    } elseif ($failed.Count -gt 0) {
        $names = ($failed | ForEach-Object { $_.Text }) -join ', '
        $text = "$($failed.Count) failed unit: $names"
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name "●  $text" -Status Critical -FontWeight 600
    } else {
        New-BGInfoLabel -Name '●  All systemd units healthy' -Status Ok `
            -FontWeight 600
    }
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Kernel' -Value $linux.Kernel
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Uptime' -Value $linux.Uptime
    if (@($linux.Load).Count -eq 3) {
        $load = "{0} · {1} · {2}  (1, 5, 15 min)" -f $linux.Load
        New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Load' -Value $load
    }
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Address' -Value $linux.Address
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Owner' -Value $linux.Owner

    # Right column: the units that matter, then what the package manager did.
    if (@($linux.Units).Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoList -Region Right -Title 'systemd units' `
            -Note "$($failed.Count) failed of $($linux.UnitCount)" `
            -Item $linux.Units
    }
    if (@($linux.Updates).Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoList -Region Right -Title 'Package updates' `
            -Item $linux.Updates
    }

    # Center: what this box answers on.
    if (@($linux.Listening).Count -gt 0) {
        $linux.Listening | New-BGInfoTable -Region Center -Title 'Listening' `
            -Note 'TCP, ss -tlnp'
    }

    # Bottom band: mounts (amber at 80 %, red at 90 %) and the load over
    # the last six hours (amber at the core count, red at 1.5 times it).
    $band = @{ Region = 'Bottom'; Height = [int](260 * $scale) }
    if ($linux.Mounts.Count -gt 0) {
        New-BGInfoChart @band -Id 'mounts' -Title 'Mounts used' `
            -Kind ProgressBar -Values @($linux.Mounts.Values) `
            -Labels @($linux.Mounts.Keys) -Maximum 100 -ValueSuffix ' %' `
            -NoProgressHandles -ShowLatestValue:$false -NoHistory `
            -ShowDataLabels -WarningThreshold 80 -CriticalThreshold 90 `
            -Width ([int](720 * $scale))
    }
    if (@($linux.LoadHistory).Count -gt 0) {
        $title = "Load average · last 6 h · $($linux.Cores) cores"
        New-BGInfoChart @band -Id 'load' -Title $title `
            -Kind Area -Values $linux.LoadHistory -Minimum 0 -ShowGrid `
            -GridLineCount 3 -ShowLatestValue -ValueFormat '0.00' -NoHistory `
            -WarningThreshold $linux.Cores `
            -CriticalThreshold ($linux.Cores * 1.5)
    }
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory `
    -OutputFileName "linux-server-$($Theme.ToLower()).png"
#endregion
